Whoa, whoa, whoa! Put away the pitchforks folks and let me explain where I'm coming from. My goal here isn't to try to invalidate anyones opinions, simple provide views based on my experience with the game to help potential buyers decide if this game is for them.
First of all, the story behind YL is intriguing. It's not Game of Thrones by any stretch, in fact it's dead simple, but it's still very interesting. I won't go into details, but let's just say that Pagies aren't just plot tokens. Keeping the out of Capital B's hands is very important to the YL - Verse (Yes, there's a YL - Verse, I was amazed too!) And Capital B may not even be the worse of YL's problems...
Next comes the title characters. It nearly hurts me say it, but I like Yooka and Laylee better than Banjo and Kazooie. Don't get me wrong. I LOVE B & K, but if I'm being honest, Yooka and Laylee make a more interesting team. Banjo was good hearted, slightly naive and, a touch lazy. Yooka is just as good hearted as Laylee,but he is more proactive, and heroic. Kazooie was snarky, hilarious, and a little bit of jerk. Laylee is all of those, (maybe a little less of a jerk) at the same time she iscrazy fun, spontanious (Just look at how she painted Bat Ship Crazy) and just a little loopy (in a good way).
Speaking of characters, ALL of them are more interesting than there BK counterparts. They aren't necessarily BETTER, but they are all more interesting. They don't feel like set pieces, or plot devices. They are written in such a way as to make it feel like they are parts of the world, not just items in it. (Since, honesty is the theme here, though, none of the Characters outshine Mumbo though, although I like Dr. Puzz a lot)
The platforming is solid, taking all of the core elements of BK and fleshing some of them out in interesting ways. Some people criticise some of the more difficult puzzles and games for their difficulty spikes breaking up the pacing, but in fairness, we've had nearly 2 decades to master the puzzles of BK, and those games had some doozies, especially when you couldn't just look up the solutions in a guide. Saying that a game like this is made worse by difficult, sometimes illogical puzzles is like complain that roguelikes don't give you enough lives. (IMHO)
BK has some of my favorite soundtracks of all time. But YL really outdoes them. While none of them have the "catchiness" of the original jingle-like tunes, they set the atmosphere for each of the worlds perfectly. The also the tunes that change when you go underwater don't just change the tempo and the instument, but seem to slightly alter the composition (It could just seem that it seems that way because the orchestral soundtracks have mroe layers) creating even cooler atmospheric effects. YL's music isn't just good video game music, it's good music period.
While I feel like most of the criticisms of this game are well summed up by Capital B. "Is this statue golden enough... Or is it too golden... Focus test it!), there are lots of legitimate criticisms of this game. If frame drops that briefly effect the asthetics, and sometimes frustrating gameplay are enough to set you off, then stay away. For five dollars you cant say much bad about this game and feel good about yourself. You get what you paid for and, to be fair, it is pretty fun. There are some pretty frustrating mechanics and flaws in the game however, but I still would say it's worth the money you spend.
Pros -
-Entertaining enough to be worth 5 dollars.
-Has a semi-helpful tutorial that explains the basics.
-Management feels relatively easy and clean.
-Graphics arent bad for five bucks, music is bearable as well.
Cons :
-Tutorial doesn't explain some key things you need to know, such as happiness management
-There is nothing you can view that I found that actually tells you why happiness is at a certain level (Maybe each pirate seperately?)
-Same Island over and over again.
-No autosave
-Remember button (To remember set ups for your fleet so you can send it back out immediately) Doesnt seem to work, or I couldn't figure it out.
-Auto assigns pirates at random to buildings it seems. So if you have unemployed level 2 pirates for your brig, and just enough to run it, you might accidentally send one of them to work somewhere on accident
-Very little information on VERY important things.
-No control over specific pirates or where they go/what they do.
-The raid menu shows a TON of items that have no explanation to what they are (I keep getting brown looking bananas. No idea what they do)
-The "Goods" section of a depot shows you everything you have. But that is the only way to see what you have over the 5 or so things at the top. Beer is important as well, as is different types of food for different levels. You get all your food crammed into one number, and only get shown rum.
Some insight into the above-
The good:
The game is pretty fun, and you'll probably be able to get your 5 dollars out of it. Rocking 2 frigates and a brig I was able to attack the third level targets, and I don't think the navy was after me yet (The navy comes after you when you become a big threat). The tutorial tells you which buildings do what.. kind of. All of this I figured out without using the tutorial, but then found it after. The building management is easy, as is resource managment. The only problem I ever actually ran into was having too MUCH of anything and having to build depots  to hold more stuff since your main building maxes out at level 3.
And the Bad:
-Let's be clear. I like this game for its price. but there are a lot of things that actually made me quitefrustrated. Lets start with the pretty useless tutorial. I expect a tutorial to explain the base game mechanics. What the tutorial does is teach you how to place the basic level buildings and build roads. That's it. No explanation on how much food each pirate eats, no explanation on what makes them happy at what level, what they need at what level, how to level them up, how to get the stuff needed to build the upgrades that ALLOW you to level them up. nothing. This isn't a huge deal, some of this stuff is easily found out by digging around in the item. But some of it isn't and I didn't find a way to figure it out before my game crashed and lost ALL of my progress to that point.
-Happiness. Let's talk about happiness. As a pirate captain, you need to keep your crew happy, or they revolt against you and game over. How do you keep them happy? No idea. The game tells you that pirates at different levels have different needs, and I assume that works into the happiness level. So build tier 2 and 3 level buildings as your pirates work up that high. Spam buildings and hope it keeps it above 60. I never got mine higher than 66, and thatwas with most of my late game buildings.
-Let's talk about population though.. The only way in this game to get more people is to kidnap them. Not a bad mechanic. But when you are lucky to get 1 or 2 people on maybe 25% of your raids, it becomes a problem. Why? Because each building takes 1 or 2 people, and as soon as you grind out enough tools (Only way to get them early is by sea) you get specialty buildings like farms and breweries and the forge. THese each need a specific thing or make a specific thing, and only that one thing at a time. A forge needs coal and iron to work. You have one quarry and one lumberjack? Make two more to produce iron and coal. A farm can only ever make one type of crop at a time, and you need 2 sometimes 3 at the same time. Spam those buildings, baby. Which would be fine in its own right, if you didn't need unemployed pirates to run your ships. 2 to a sloop, your best option early (the brig is largely useless at this stage) and you need about 4 sloops or so to hit 100% success on a village I believe. Thats 8 people you can never have working if you want to (and you NEED to) raid.
This gets worse later game when the buildings poach seemingly random pirates to run buildings. Have a crew of level 2's to run your brig? Pray to rnjesus they don't get pulled into a building you give workers.
Acquiring new people does get easier once you get later into the buildings, and you can later spam levels so it doesn't much matter who gets pulled. But it seems like a broken mechanic to me.
- No autosave means you are at the mercy of crashes. I don't know why I didn't expect a game like this (no offense) to crash, but I didn't give it much thought. I was only 2 hours in and, boom. All gone.
-The menu showing you what you get after a raid is pretty useless. In 1920x1080, the icons were so small you could only recognize stuff you see all the time. Cannonballs are round. The other 60 or so items, I have no idea what they are, and you can't mouse over them to see an item name. Useless menu.
-The Goods menu on the top. You need different food and different drink for different level pirates, I'm assuming. That's how I *think* the mechanics work. All your food is lumped together into one big number, so maybe that doesn't matter? Rum is the only drink shown, so maybe once you can make that nothing else matters? You get shown clothes, but I am unsure what those do, since running at 0 doesnt seem to make anyone unhappy and having a ton doesnt make anyone MORE happy. Planks and rocks are shown, so that's good. Weapons are not, and you need those to level up.
-The remember button in the Raid section does nothing as far as I can tell.
Rant over. It's a good game if you don't expect much out of it.

First of all: I've seen a lot of people comparing this game with Tropico 2. And since I don't have it, I won't be able to make a good comparison; but there are perspectives worth looking at.
1. The graphic: Please, what do you really expect from a game that's just a little bit expensive than a smartphone game? Still a lot of room to improve though (e.g. the raiding scene with the ships leaving the port, instead of just having one ship model with different masts, it would probably be better to have different ship models for different missions to prevent boredom)
2. The sound: Not bad, although it does sounds quite cheap, But again, for 5 bucks it is already a decent service.
3. The gameplay: Very linear: gather resources, raid, repeat. You'd probably stopped playing after a couple of hours, BUT in comparison to big names like the Anno series (I've tried 1404 and 2070) or Banished mods, the production chain in this game are a lot easier to master; the tier 3 buildings rarely need a lot of tier 2 or tier 1 building to function properly, which makes the game easier to learn.
Probably the biggest turn-offs in this game is the multiple repetition: You started on the same island, the same resources, the same starting place, and progress the same way.
BUT, knowing how these small budget games work, I might predict the futureof this game: MODS. A lot of it. Yes, it might make the game more difficult, but if this game want to be much more playable, the developer DEFINITELY have to let ppl make mods for this game, ranging from small graphic changes to a new resource chain and new ship types.
Still; a fast food meal set would probably cost the same (or a couple bucks more expensive) but it'll just fill your stomach for a short time; this game, because of its simplicity could be played again and again, even between short one-hour break.
In the end, this game really worth the 5 euro or 5 dollars spending, and I'd like to spend another 5 euro for more content, like easy misisons, more maps, more ship texture, and a couple of small extensions. Prost for the developers! :D

Browsing the many booths at Anime Central in Chicago, one card game caught my friend's eye. It stood out from all the other card games because it featured pixel art, and the box was reminiscent of a NES game box. So we picked it up and took it home with us. We had such a blast playing it and sharing it with other friends. That card game was Boss Monster.

Imagine my excitement when I found out a digital version was coming to Steam, with online multiplayer.

The digital version isn't  perfect, but for an early access title it's pretty solid. It's rather easy to pick up if you're familiar with the card game. If you haven't played then you might be turned away by the sudden wall of text you have to read which is the tutorial, but once you get it down and play a few rounds it begins to make sense.

There are many options and possibilities for different kinds of dungeons. Some will work well with your boss character, some will not. It's also possible to get a really unlucky hand and just be stuck at the bottom the entire game, but it rarely happens. You win some and you lose some.

A couple things I would personally like to see is a better tutorial which teaches through experience rather then having to memorize text, and an option to turn off the timer in multiplayer as it gets a little annoying sometimes, especially if you're fairly new to the game.

Overall it's a fun game that deserves to be played. Buy it, play it, love it.

Tired of playing the good guy? I feel you, my friend. If you are looking for some place to fight some heroes, luring them into your deadly traps or cast some mighty (and again, deadly) spells, Boss Monster might be the right choice. But be aware, the other Monsters aren’t your allies so don’t expect them to help you.
Let’s get started quickly. At first, choose between single - or multiplayer. You can play worldwide, invite friends, play hot seat or simply fight against the AI. Picking your boss monster comes next. We have Mummy Cleopatra, Xyzax the Lich, Seducia the Siren and many more, each with a unique Special Ability that can be activated only once every game. So what is the Main Goal of every match? To win, you have to be the first boss that collected 10 Hero Souls and to do so you have to slay, of course, heroes. But be aware, heroes making it through your sidescrolling dungeon will hit you with 1 wound, epic heroes even 2 wounds. To make sure that you don’t take the maximum of 5 wounds and die, playing your cards wisely is inevitable. Build rooms, use synergies, activate abilities and cast spells if necessary. Heroes need to be attracted, that’s why every room has at least one Treasure Icon. If you see that there is a mage in town and you want to lure him, build more rooms with a spellcasting icon. Same goes for fighters, clerics and thieves. The game comes with a tutorial, right before the first match or always available in the settings, making me stop the basic overview now.
Boss Monster delivers old-school 8-Bit Graphics and a NES-like Soundtrack that tends to get annoying after a while. The virtual cards look great and have funny descriptions, the same goes for heroes and our beloved villains. But some issues affected my gameplay and are already discussed in the forum. Just to mention some: The game has been released for iPad as well and thus suffers from a bad resolution in terms of Text-Boxes and general User Interface. The overall gameplay seems to be slow since you can interfere with every move heroes or opposing bosses perform. To do so you always have to check different buttons instead of just playing cards like spells that can be instantly performed, meaning Clicks, Clicks, Clicks…
Playing with more than 1 opponent means you have to click on the other icons to check the rooms they built, since there are only 2 bosses displayed at once. Playing solo is fun indeed but the lack of story condemns Boss Monster to be a game best enjoyed in Multi-Player. Thus I tried to enter a worldwide match, waiting for 45 mins until I cancelled the queue. Let’s sum it up.
My inner demons are still fighting while writing this so I should make it clear. I recommend this game, yes. For its idea, its “easy to learn, hard to master” gameplay and the overall retro-look, sound and artwork.
This game is still in Early Access and needs not only lots of improvements regarding UI and getting rid of all these unnecessary clicks it took over from the mobile port but also more content for solo-players. Devs are working on Bugs, crashes people were talking about didn’t occur for me while playing about 10 games, so progress is happening. Gather your friends and invite them to online matches and increase the worldwide player-base or take your girl/boyfriend and hate each other in a Hot Seat match.
If you are not sure about it, don’t buy it now, wait for a sale instead. 6,99 Seems to be more of a future investment than a price that reflects its current state.
6/10

I thought this looked interesting, and the concept seems good, then I started playing it.
First bad sign: not being able to choose what monster you play as. Having my "character" selected completely at random was weird.
Then there was the less than intuitive system for starting a game. It LOOKS like everything is locked out, but in fact allowed me to start a game as long as I did not select any of the game modes that it showed. I had to be higher level to unlock those... apparently...
The games rules are explained only in a slideshow thing, which does NOT help me to remember the rules. Maybe other people are fine with it, but it left me either having to drop back to the main menu, or go to the internet to look up rules.
Interface was odd, often requiring you to click on things you might not expect in order to proceed, and a misclick takes you back, or worse: advances the turn without you taking an action.
AI seemed good for the opponent, but it rapidly became apparent that it was either cheating, or just lucky ALL the time. I almost won twice. The first time, I had half my health left, and in the middle of the AIs turn, with a hero stomping up the middle of its' dungeon, the screen flickered and announced that I had lost, game over. The second time, with the AI a single move short of losing its' last point of health, and me still having ALL my health, the game abruptly closed itself.
Maybe there are bugs being fixed, and maybe the rules will be better explained, but between all that and the startlingly limited number of cards I could find in the game, this feels like a party wipe.

I'm going to give this a 5/10 at the moment.  The content that is present is well done and relatively stable/bug free.  Ship combat is fun for a while, and space is visually interesting with a few suprises.  But get a few hours in and the game starts to feel kind of pointless.
There is a faction system, but it doesn't do much of anything.  There is trading and mining, but neither give money at anywhere near the rate fighting does.  There are generated "missions", but they are extremely easy and give very little in the way of rewards (you'll probably do them just to have something to do).  There are enemy bases and structures, but you can't destroy them (you can get them to one health and they just hang there, and frankly it isn't hard at all to do that).  You end up collecting money to buy a bigger ship to collect more money to buy an even bigger ship (which isn't very rewarding, as the ship models are so small in relation to one another you dont get the sense that you have a bigger ship)...
The game isn't garbage, and the devs are very nice and responsive.  At $5-$10 give it a shot, but not at $40.  The caveat here is there is a very soid framework to make a much better game (really this game is in the bin with so many others that are really in early-mid beta, but release early to make money).  If there is a content update that adds player bases and the ability to capture territory, balances out mining and trading, and puts in other end-game content and empire building mechanics, this game will be a 9/10 easy.  It feels like these things were intended, but just haven't made it in.  So, if you see a big update after this review, maybe give it a try.  Otherwise, skip it until there is a big steam sale (or skip entirely, if a space grind isn't your thing).

Star Point Gemin 2 is a fantasic starship space genre game that will have you playing for hours on end. I’ve spent more than 60 hours with the game at this point and I’ve only just scratched the surface. I’ve primarily been playing in the games “free roam” mode as that was the real draw of the game for me. I knew from the outset that I wanted a game that gave me the ability to explore, fight, mine and trade at my own leisure and do so in my own ship like a “real” space captain. After researching SPG2 a bit I realized that this would be the game that would allow me to do all of that.
I’m not a diehard space sim player so games like EVE Online and Star Trek Online have always kind of intimidated me. I’ve never really had an interest in the X3 series (my loss probably) but I have played Sins of a Solar Empire and the Homeworld series. It's been a while since I've played anything space related but lately I’ve become re-interested in the genre with games like Star Citizen and Elite: Dangerous on the horizon. I knew I wanted to play a game that felt huge and expansive but I didn’t want to play a game that made me feel like a small fish in a huge pond. I’m a casual player so the size and scope of this game feels just right to me. The game's setting is huge and there is a lot to do in it. Also, it seems like the devs are really committed to making the game better all the time which made the choice to buy it all the more easy to make. The fact that I’ve continued to play it so much is a testament to how good it actually is.
SPG2 reminds me specifically of two games I’ve played before, Nexus: The Jupiter Incident and Star Trek: Starfleet Command. Although I’ve played many other space genre games since, I really wanted to play something that felt similar to those two games. SPG2 has a surprising amount in common with Starfleet Command which also allowed you to “tractor beam” aka grapple ships, scan anomalies and commandeer other spacecraft with “marines” aka troopers. I haven’t played that game in over 15 years but I remember how much fun it was to do those things in the game.
These are some of the things I like about SPG2:
-	the music is great especially the main theme
-	the ship designs are cool and I know there are still tons more to discover
-	the space station designs are great and varied which is a plus
-	the variety of weapons and their FX in game look great
-       the descriptions for items and npcs in the game are numerous and often amusing
-       there are many mods availiable which help to enhance gamplay
The randomness of missions and enemies is great but whether or not you like this aspect of the game will depend on how much you like doing things in this universe. After awhile the missions can seem repetitive but luckily the fact that the level required to do each mission changes all the time, forces you to decide which missions to do or not to do. This in turn helps mix things up a bit and keep things interesting.
The only issues I have with the game so far are the way the menus in stations and on planets were a bit confusing at first and still seem a bit cumbersome to navigate. Also I wish there was a bit more 'humanity' in the game. By that I just mean it would be cool if officers had portraits in addition to their names and when ships attacked you they too had portraits instead of just insignias. I know that's a huge 'ask' as there are already a huge amount of randomized officer names in the game. Perhaps a feature that allowed you upload your own portraits to the game (specifically for officers) could be cool. Also, I’m not entirely sure, but I think officers gain experience the longer they are on your ship. I hope so but it would also be cool if they could steadily gain loyalty for additional bonuses.
Other than that I’ve really enjoyed this game and am glad I bought it.

Having put 40 hours into multiplayer at the time of writing I will just get straight to the point. This CoD can be fun to play and intensely competetive, however it this is overshadowed by without a doubt in my mind the worst community I have ever seen in ANY video game. I see people always whining, calling people names, hacking accusations seemingly more because they were bested than because they were actually hacking - on this point I'd also like to point out theres quite a number of very good/serious players that will abuse killstreaks and spawns, especially if you end up on nuketown or hijacked and get very high kill games. (if you are on the recieving end, you have my sympathy) This is something I find pretty common in the NukeJacked playlist.
Just before I had people seriously having a go at me because I decided to use an lmg. And apparently I was camping. Except we were playing a game mode where you have to capture and defend an objective (hardpoint) and the hypocrite did the same thing to me anyway! The community is just generally not what you would call mature, and the text chat will get annoying if you have it enabled. I imagine voip is the same but I have it off, not expecting anything better.
Besides the community the multiplayer isn't what you could call balanced either. As mentioned, spawns can be manipulated - particuarly on certain, smaller maps. This can be extremely frustrating as you can be effectively spawntrapped, and not even by a team of co-ordinated people! Killstreaks, while fun can similarly completely destroy your chances in a match if the enemy gets and starts using higher killstreaks on you.
If you can ignore these things, then this can be really fun, fast paced and competetive. But I can't recommend this game baring in mind the things I've mentioned.

What were the developers thinking?
You get two choices before the game starts: Freelance and Campaign.
The game clearly says you can choose to do the campaign and then roam around the galaxy doing whatever you want and restart the campaign again when you feel like it.
If you choose Freelance, that's what you're stuck with.  You cant start the campaign from inside a freelance game.  Ok, no problem with that.
I chose to do campaign and then jump into freelance, 5 minutes into the campaign you get the choice to continue it or go freelance.  Now any normal person would assume that this was a choice INSIDE the campaign mode.
Nope, it kicks you out to freelance mode so you spend two days having fun flying around, decide it's time to continue with the main story and find it's not there.
You think it must be ANOTHER bug (Alpha release? Really guys?) so do some googling only to find out for the Devs know about it and seem to consider it a feature.  I like this game but I want my two days back.
I'm going to reach into the future and recommend this game to future readers of this comment, I think it's going to be something great.  For right now though save your money.

This is a game like X3 where you fly around in space and can take on a lot of roles, trader, pirate, etc.  The game is pretty and the space scenes are very nice.  The graphics are smooth and pretty interesting.  The game itself is pretty boring.  I usually play as a trader/adventurer in X3.  So, the ships are all pretty boring and the number systems you can use in them is not very interesting either.  Basically, there are different types of weapons you can mount but they are all pretty much the same.  The game tries to make them interesting by using mods and personal skills but it's too complex (there is very little documentation) and too simple (basically every mod is just a slight variation in the effect of the weapon).  The ships are the same way, they get bigger and badder, but the bad guys scale right up too so you basically just fly around and each mission is about the same.  There are a very limited number of missions in the game and you either tranport cargo, a vip, assassinate a bad guy, or repair a station.  All are very very easy to complete even when you choose ones marked hard.  Every now and then someone just flat takes you out but there is no middle ground.  After about 20 hours, it's just the same thing over and over again.  Trade is very simplistic and since it doesn't really cost you anything to fly around, you just buy low and sell high.  The worst part is the cost.  Ships and weapons cost a fortune but missions and trade generates very little per outing so it takes thousands of missions to generate a new ship.  Resale values are ridiculously low (for instance a ship that costs 10 million credits has a sale value of about 2M).  The only way to really make money is to cap ships.  That works.  The bad news is, that is hard to do effectively since there is little to no control over your other units in combat and they just shoot up everything.  The flight controls are awful.  Using the keyboard you have all these other combat mods that are hard to use and limited.  Mostly, there is no documention of anything so you don't really know what to do.  The tutorial is just some tidbits that get so annoying you turn it off.  Bottom line, this game is boring and has no depth.  Maybe mods will add to it in the future, but for now I got over it pretty fast.

So...my main interest in playing this game was due to the numerous talk of how amazing the story was. I went into it with no idea of what I was getting into except for a third person shooter that actually has some substance in its narrative. With that said I was dropped off on the outskirts of Dubai controlling Captain Martin Walker and accompanied by two other Delta operatives Adams and Lugo.
The story starts off pretty simple and straightforward, but slowly reveals the layers and characters that are involved in the chaos that permeates throughout Dubai. I found myself hooked from the beginning as Captain Walker's squad is constantly trying to get some understanding and control of what is happening around them. I can't remember what chapter, maybe 10 or 11, but Colonel Konrad said something that for the first time ever in a third or first person shooter did I find myself questioning if the decisions and path I had been taking was the right one. Hands down one of the best and most engaging stories I've ever played, regardless of genre.
Gameplay wise it's your standard third person cover shooter. There are a variety of weapons to utilize (assault rifles, pistols, shotguns, sniper rifles, etc.) throughout your "heroic" mission. If I had to compare it to another game in terms of how it felt I would say Army of Two.
I would recommend to buy it during a sale though. As amazing as the story is, the game as a whole is not worth the $29.99 it is priced as of the posting of this review. My first play through was on the Combat Ops difficulty which I would equate to a medium setting and I beat the game in less than 6 hours. With the campaign being short there is a multiplayer and co-op mode, but they don't add a whole lot.
Overall a great story and soundtrack with average gameplay and little extra features. Grab it when it's under $10 and see if you feel like a hero at the end of it all.

So, I love the tabletop version of this game.
The digital.. does not shine yet the way one would like. The PC version is a shoddy port of the mobile version that has clunky controls that require a dozen clicks for everything, and everything is all 'click and drag through'- i'm sure it's OK on a touch screen but FFS this is the PC port, better mouse support!
Then comes the port of paper to digital. Let's be honest here: Boss Monster is not a game you ('most gamers') will sit down specifically to play. It's what we call a filler game. Waiting for Pizza, 'couple players in the D&D group are late.. any time there's a bit of time to fill, you can break it out and have a few minutes of silly fun.
There is precisely ONE benefit of the digital edition over the physical edition: the price. Outside of that, there's NO reason to go digital.
There's not a lot of synergy and strategy to the game, so the digital doesn't help you 'practice'.
There's not a lot of convoluted maths that the digital edition streamlines.
The mechanics are not particularly engaging, nor are they complicated.
There isn't a real 'story' to the game.
There's not much in the way of fun graphics.
In other words, this is a PC port of a mobile port of a tabletop card game, and it plays just like a tabletop filler card game, without any real advantage over the tabletop edition.
Also, the only expansion so far that's out, requires you to win the game /40/ times to get? Blood hell. I'm not sure I've actually played the tabletop edition 40 times yet, and definitely haven't won it 40 times.
It occurs to me that this game is still in early access, and the developers might read reviews looking for things that need improvements, so I will add some things which could change my rating:
Improved UI with better mouse support.
A few less clicks to accomplish basic tasks. (The 'halt' button, for example is needless, there should be a countdown bar with 4 options: Play spell, use room, go, go-all.)
The ability to select the boss you play, or at least get dealt a new one.
Ability to increase the game speed.
Allowance of 'house rules' (increase/decrease hand size, alter starting card distribution, alter souls/wounds required to win/lose, etc.)

Playing Yooka-Laylee by Team17 and Playtonic Games I was immediately reminded of sitting on my family couch in the basement with my brother, eating Little Debbie snacks and playing Spongebob Squarepants: Battle for Bikini Bottom on our PS2. It’s a formula you’ll recognize if you played platform games as a kid. You’ll find hidden treasure chests if you explore. You’ll learn new moves to unlock more areas of gameplay. The villains (like Dr. Quack and Capital B) are outlandish and extreme. And, you’ll definitely recognize the camera panning across the platform challenge course to the shiny prize at the end. It’s a tried and true method, and it’s just as fun now as it was in my childhood basement sitting on the family couch – though I wouldn’t say the same for the Little Debbies.
Like our favorite games from childhood, Yooka-Laylee has personality, strange and amusing characters, and tons of collectibles. You play as a bat and a lizard named Yooka and Laylee who run around collecting “Pagies” and “Quills,” both in the hub world and in five additional worlds that you unlock once you’ve collected enough Pagies. As you may have noticed, this game is a not-so-subtle homage to Banjo-Kazooie, but it seems designed for players nostalgic for platform games in general. The puzzles are satisfying and creative, involving different moves and skills you acquire throughout your gameplay. The different worlds are amusing and actually pretty extensive compared to Banjo-Koozie. And though it’s possible I had so much fun with this game because it deftly tapped into my nostalgia, I think the challenges, levels, and puzzles are diverse and interesting enough to be fun for anyone.

Great game from the the prologue and first episode releasted. It feels alot like the old style hitman jumping back to Blood Money, the way i think hitman should be. Despite there only being one level excluding the prologue it is huge and i find myself finding a new way to navigate it and kill my targets each time with new weapons etc. I would strongly reccomend the game i have had no performance issues which i did have in the Beta so its nice to see those have been sorted.
Pros
- Going back to the original idea of hitman. Non-linear levels which you can explore at your own pace finishing off your targets however you want.
- I havent had any problems with running it on decent settings with my 770 alot of people have complained about it being locked to Low but if you ramp up the rest of the settings it still looks flawless,
- Huge amount of replayablility there. With escalation missions adding a new hurdle each time you play a level to just exploring parts of a level you never even ventured into in the first place. Theres a huge number of ways to complete each level.
- Good amount of options and graphical settings along with being able to rebind all your keyboard functions if needed.
Cons
- Episodic release so even with the huge amount of replayablility expect to be left wanting more which you wont get till April. Think of it as a long term investmant if you go for the Full Experience not just you buying a game now.
- Always Online feature has seen me be kicked from the game losing progress telling me i lost my connection despite my connection being fine and it seeming to be the Hitman Servers. Meaning that certain content cant be downloaded and ran offline. Its a pain and the only thing for me that really retracts from this being the perfect hitman game.
In all i would strongly reccomend the game Agent 47 once again feels like he has a strong presence and meaning whilst also the game understanding that he is not a one man army and does need to utilise stealth and his surrounds to succeed in each mission, unlike in Absolution where you could find yourself easily shooting your way through a level if wanted.I understand alot of people have had performance issues but i havent so be wary of this and maybe go for the Intro pack or even just petition for refund on steam if it does not run for you.

You fly around in a 3rd person /behind/ view of a ship and you navigate through space by an interactive 2D starmap.  You do missions, which are mainly destroy other ships or follow the main campaign , which is pretty much flying to various location and ...drumroll...destroy other ships.
The way it's done is by trying to position your ship so your main guns get the best angle and this requires moving your camera view while keeping an eye on your speed and direction.   Also don't forget to activate your "powers", which are usually about your shields, your guns or extra chance to hit ...similar abilities you'd find in many fantasy rpgs.
While this may be fun for many...and the argument of "but so are other similar games have a similar gameplay" , this game doesn't really push any boundaries.   You could easily see it as a copycat of Starflight from the late 80s, but that had more features (planetary landing and exploration).
The game just feels shallow, despite the best attempts and best intentions of the developers and there is a huge thumb up for their efforts and communication with the public while making this game, but I'm here to write a review on the game, not the intentions and public relations.

tl;dr Early Access First Impressions: A very faithful port of the physical game with a somewhat unintuitive UI that does little to explain itself to the player. Worth buying if you're a fan of the game or have been interested in it.
---
(Note that this is from the perspective of someone who owns and enjoys the physical game. The review is a combination of the actual game and its port.)
For the card game itself...
Do you like casual card games? Do you like sprite art? Do you often get nostalgic over the 8-bit and 16-bit platformer days? You'll probably like Boss Monster. It's a fairly simple game where you play as - well, a boss monster in a video game. Your goal is to build a dungeon that can both attract and kill any heroes dumb enough to step foot in it while competing against other boss monsters attempting to do the same.
Besides building your dungeon, you also have access to spells that can change the outcome of the game dramatically if used properly by buffing heroes in another boss' dungeon, disabling their rooms so they can't affect the hero and so on. Every room has an affect of its own that can sometimes interact with other rooms within your dungeon, offering a decent amount of strategic options for placement without really racking the brain too much.
Overall, it's an extremely fun casual game to play with friends and relax with. It makes a great 'opening' or 'closing' game to a board/card game night and it's highly recommended from me.
As for the port...
It's adequate. It has a large amount of visual polish and the tutorial is sufficient in teaching a new player how to play. The UI is a bit unintuitive, however, as it does very little to offer feedback to the player. The tutorial does nothing to explain the UI either and makes it a bit worse and leaves the player to sort of poke around until they figure it out for themselves... which may involve a destroyed room or discarded card on accident. The UI was pretty clearly made with touch screens in mind first and PC players a distant second. The little summaries of all of the bosses are quite nice and help keep track of the game state very well.
That all said, though, it isn't exactly a puzzle. Most of the functionality is fairly obvious. Want to use a card's effect? Click it. It does lack solid visual feedback for selecting cards - especially at the beginning of a game where you need to discard two cards from your hand. In the case of a dungeon with a lot of traps, activating the effect of one trap room immediately sends you back to the card selection screen without any positive indicator that you've actually activated it until you click OK. More feedback as to what the player's selections and actions are would be nice.
Another thing is the Halt button. It's unnecessary and misleading. Clicking it actually doesn't immediately halt the game - it just presents options, including probably the most important one of all: Pass All. This skips all of your actions for the current dungeon being adventured through. If you have no spell cards in hand and it's currently your opponent's adventuring turn, for example, there is no reason for you to stop the game. If more people knew about this, the games would go SIGNIFICANTLY faster. Rather than have the Halt button, just make the three options (Play A Card, Pass Once, Pass All) visible throughout the entirety of the adventuring phase.
Overall, these are mostly minor issues that don't detract from the experience overly much. Since the game is still in early access, I expect the developer to make a few passes over the UI before its 'actual' release. What's here now, though, is perfectly playable and still enjoyable. It's still Boss Monster. It is not integrated into Steamworks and goes purely through their own servers (likely to prepare for crossplatform play similar to Ascension,) but online play has so far been smooth for me. I haven't tested inviting friends to private games yet nor have I tried the hotseat play option so take this review for what it is: a first impressions review.

Do you like strategy games? Do you like survival games, that aren't early access zombie games? do you like a challange? Then this game is for you!
Oxygen Not Included shows a new side of strategic survival with a category that has never been seen before
Stranded underground on an asteroid, you and your brave duplicants need to fight the odds to survive as long as you can, but it will not be easy, you will have to find oxygen, provide food and water, electricity, and health.
This game is getting progressivly harder for every upgrade that is released, by adding to the complexity, in the means of farming, or health. It has great potential to become one of the best survival games out there, without a doubt.
If the support for modding is introduced, which it currently isn't, it will raise the game into new highs, it would fit in well, and allow for the creation of even more challanges, or to make the game easier, for those who wants that.
The game has a unique art style, and gameplay, a 2D gameplay, with amazing depth (pun intended) It shows mechanics never seen before, and it is well done, while other games who introduce new gameplay might fail in creating it properly, this game does it right.
It is an amazing game, but it is early access, so it has its flaws and bugs;
The gameplay quickly becomes repetetive, since there is currently no goal, other than surviving for as long as you can. This is not a big issue, as it has an easy fix, simply give yourself challanges, find other's challanges, or experiment with new ways to plan or build. Recently new items have been added to the game which shows more of a story line, in the form of structures which the player has not built. The developers are currently working on a backstory/story to the game, and I am very excited to see where they take this.
The AI of the duplicants is not the best, good, but not the best. They frequenlty get them self stuck, walk into pits, drown themselves, and the pathfinding is not the best. This is improving however, simply by the time I bought this game, it has improved a lot.
This certainly is one of my favorite games, and has a special place in my heart, it is a concept done well, and has amazing potential
TL;DR
Pros:
Good mechanics
New concept
Versitility
Challanging yourself
Modding, hopefully soon
Cons:
Currently no story (is planned to be added)
AI is not the best (but is improving)
Summary: Very good game with loads of potential, cheap for the amount of gameplay you get, a must play if you like strategy/survival!

Where to start... The game itself requires some minor polish, mainly in the balancing sector, but it's already at a very good/stable state otherwise. There are various tasks to do inside the game, such as exploration, boarding ships, mining, trading(These do still need balancing.) and ofcourse, the campaign mode and pewpew fighting.
The game is fairly complex, once you start getting into it, learning to fly and maneuver different ship classes, the firing arcs of various ships, finding fighting tactics that work for you and your ship, the enhancement system... And for those who get bored quickly after having played through the storyline, which did happen to a lot of players in other games such as Freelancer, you do have a nice amount of achievements to hunt, some of which aren't exactly easy to accomplish. Nothing is stopping you from hunting down the "Heros" either. ;)
The community and the devs are active and communicating a lot, which reflects into the product and the pace patches, fixes and balancing attempts are coming through. There are plans for an expansion and DLC, which will further add to the amount of content in the game and ofcourse, the community made mods, which will be the crowning jewel of this game. The tools might not be fully functional yet, but as soon as the game itself is at a state where the devs and community are happy, the tools will be recieving some much needed love.
A lot has been said about the game in many of the reviews, but here's another list of just some of the features already in the game and some which are being worked on:
Already in:
-Boarding Ships.
-Working Campaign.
-Lots and lots of ships.
-Weapon/ship system enhancement.
-Trading.
-Dynamic events which effect item prices.
-A large amount of space to explore, which can also be further expanded.
-Lots of different factions.(Which will also get some more love in the future.)
-Freeroam mode for those who don't wish to play the campaign.
-Mercenaries to act as your backup.
-Blueprints.
-Working collision system.
-Cloaking!
-Heroes to hunt,
-Mods.
Planned/in the works:
-Player owned faction and base(s).
-Dynamic struggles for power/regional control between factions. Once this is implemented, every single playthrough will be and feel different!
-Expansion/DLC.
-Modding Tools.(Currently some work, some don't. Somewhat prone to crashes.)
-Improvements to the HUD and other elements of the UI.
-An entirely new ship class.(Larger, naturally. Bigger is always better!)
... and the list goes on.
If you aren't a fan of space sims or dislike games with emphasis on exploration, this might not be for you, as there is no MP in the game to increase its lifespan. However, if you do like what you've seen/read and can get past the fact that there is no MP and that the game relies entirely on mods/expansions/DLC to keep breathing fresh life into it, then this game just might be a perfect fit for you. Atleast I've completely fallen in love with the game.

After months waiting for the game to finally run properly with a lot of patching, I finally got to play the game smoothly on my computer. And after buying the upgrade pack, I turn my thumb down into a recommandation.
Hitman hits a sweet spot between Blood Money and Absolution...closer (way closer) to Blood Money though. Each episode revolves around a big (fat) map, one place where you have to take down multiple targets. That means that Io Interactive understood that focusing on a lousy, vulgar, annoying and stupid plot like Absolution wasn't a good idea. And that instead focusing on level-design was the key to make a good Hitman again. And good it is.
+ The comeback of good level-design:
The new maps are not only bigger than the fourth entry in the series - that at the time had some impressive crowded environments like the carnaval - but they also keep the level of density and details in terms of interactions with the environement that previous games had. Discovering these maps could have been a bit overwhelming, but Io Int found a clever enough way to have the player complete de mission at least once, being rewarded by the successful kills, but always tickling the curiousity, pushing the player to come back and doing the mission in a different way. They kind of went for the Absolution route on this: you almost always have a really easy option that present itself to you in the first few minutes walking in the level. That option is often viable, and leads to another one, but is rarely the most fun and/or challenging way to progress into the level. Sapienza for example gives you the opportunity to enter the villa as a cook, less than 30 seconds after entering the zone. But you can find at least 5 or 6 other ways just to get in (not even counting the ways to kill the two targets). Same goes for most of the missions.
That means the player is, more than ever in the series, pushed to replay the same missions over and over to find all the fun ways to get to the targets. This is also encouraged by the interface that lets the player know at the end of each mission that he/she still has so many ways to dress up, or so many ways to kill a target. Though it gets a bit ridicullous in terms of numbers, these little challenge like "Kill the target with a shuriken" or "Drown the target" makes for a good replay value. And since the levels are so big and dense, it actually works for most mission.
+ A find balance for  AIs:
The game also deals with the stupid instinct from Absolution, while also addressing the incoherence of never being spotted while costumed in the first four episodes. Absolution had you not using disguise (the soul of these games) because it was way to risky, even unplayable to be surrounded by people with the same disguise...whitch kind of made sense sometimes (like being dressed as a chinese cook) but not at all some othe time (like being dressed as a cop a large crime scene involving several police reinforcement). Hitman 2016 choose something between never being caught and always being caught. Some characters are more knowledgable than others, meaning they will know who their employees are and will spot you if you get close enough. But most of the people won't catch on you costume if you don't act like an idiot.
The game also prevent the insta-death/chase when the player gets spotted, simply by having most of the IAs pushing you toward the exit if spotted, instead of being extremelly aggressive. That means that the player has bit more room to try some things without having to rely to much on quick save and reload. Kudos for that too.
- A bit short? Sort of? I don't know:
Some missions, like Sapienza, almost feel like glorious remakes of previous levels (in that case the first one from Hitman: Silent Assassin) without ever feeling like they are completely out of ideas. But honestly, having only six levels feel a bit short of an experience, even though the quality is here, I can't help but think that a part of the content is not as fun as a new mission could be. The escalation mode is not my cup of tea, and since the ellusive targets, which is a great idea by the way, can't be played if you missed them the time they were available, I feel like I'm missing a mission or two to be fully satisfied by what is available for this first season...
+ - A bit more serious:
This part is more debatable than anything I wrote before. I think that Absolution went way too stupid, sexist, ridiculous and vulgar. The plot managed to have incoherences in every single cutscene and since the game wanted so much for the player to follow that story, pushing it forward, it was even more of a shore to look at it. On the other hand plots never was really great in Hitman.
For this one, Io Int embrace a more, if not serious, at least more elegant tone. It feels like a James Bond from the Craig's era. Everything from the cold yet soft cinematography, to the alternate suits that 47 wears by default instead of his iconic black suit and red tie (that you can still choose while preparing for the mission), to the plot resembling more a spie flick than anything else; it smells Bond, and it suits the series perfectly...Except it doesn't have a really talkative 47 or a charismatic cast overall. The overall character design, set design and mission design are really fine in my opinion. But if you want to get rid of the "dress like a big red bird and stop the vice president from being killed in the middle of a drunk as s*** crowd" sort of atmosphere, you need to bring the charisma back in another way.
That is where I think the season 2 would benefit from a bit more "dialogues" as a mechanic in the game. Being able to talk to people more than a handful of instances in specific circonstances would be great. That would let us hear 47 speak a bit more, using his charismatic voice, and maybe having just a little bit more banter and fun in the presentation (without going overboard with it). As it is, we don't even have the dialogues between him and Diana at the beginning of the mission, since she speaks on her own during the brieffing and during the intro of the mission.
TL;DR
I love it.
At least two of the six main missions are in my top 10 missions from the series (most of this top 10 coming from Blood Money) and only one felt mediocre. The scale and quality in the level design is there and the few tweaks in the AIs are very welcome. It lacks a bit of charisma, feels a bit cold at time in terms of art direction, but it is pretty damn good.

Borderlands 2, 9.7/10
Sure, my playtime isn't as much as a lot of gamers' profiles, but, I have played this game enough to know that it's replay value is very high. With 4 different characters to choose from (6 with DLC), you have that many different playstyles to run rampant with. Gunzerker if you liked Brick from the first Borderlands game, Commando if you like deploying a turret-shield, Assassin if you like sniping/sneaking/melee (and haikus), and lastly, Siren if you really like being a badass while looking the part. With the DLC, you can also be a Psycho, because buzzsaws, explosives, and being on fire is really friggin sweet, and you can also be a Mechromancer (my favorite), for those of you who want to avenge all of your missed bullets (or if you want to see what it's like to miss) in a blaze of OP explosive glory while your Deathtrap lights everyone else on fire.
There is literally so much to do! For those that don't mind buying DLC (or playing DnD), Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep is a harder storyline that levels the enemies up as you do, some will level in combat! Beyond that, you could literally just walk around Pandora and kill everything in your path and return to Sanctuary to turn in all of the accidental quests you completed and become rich!
I really recommend this to beginning gamers. With wave after wave of quickly moving enemies, it betters your FPS reflexes, and teaches you the importance of melee. A quick, triple-shot rapid fire from a high damage Jacobs weapon followed by a melee attack is (for me) one of the best combos out there. Of course, if playing as Mechromancer, your best option is to empty your clip and get that Anarchy damage bonus for the next clip. Or, if playing as Psycho, just run in there guns blazing and buzzsaws whirring to take everybody out. There are so many ways of finishing off a cluster of 25+ enemies that it ends up sharpening your gaming mind with agile and adaptive thinking skills.
One thing wrong with the game is the repetitiveness, but all of that is quickly cleared up by Handsome Jack's dialogue (or monologue) and the fact that you probably have the most OP gun for your level at that point.
All in all, it's a great game, and also my personal favorite for one to go back to every so often.

A brilliant game I've been following for about a year now, I believe. Updates every month with loyal, funny devs (if you watch the update videos), that are obviously affected by feedback. First off, it's very relieving with devs that doesn't abandon the game early on, good job devs!
Now, for the the review:
Gameplay 9/10:
As you probably know, this game revolves around designing a prison. The first impression was the immense freedom of choice. There's limitless ways of constructing your prison (check the workshop for this game if you want examples, also, the game has Steam Workshop!).
Beginning to the game, it's a bit difficult, but you can adjust difficulty indirectly through what prisoners you would take in to the prison (minimum risk, medium risk, maximum risk, and any combinations of these). It also remain a challenge later on, due to characteristics of inmates, such as "strong", "deadly", "snitch" etc.
Generally, the game is fun, with a lot of variety, details, that makes the game worth the price. Indeed, the price is somewhat above the usual indie game price, but in my opinion, the game was worth it (you can check the hours on record with most players is above 20, including the negative reviews).
Graphics 10/10:
Of course, it's an indie game, and I won't review it as an AAA title regarding graphics. The visuals are charming in its' own way, and the dogs are really cute. But mainly, the most important aspect of why I granted max score on this topic is due to smart programming. The game doesn't require much, and I've played the game on laptops and stationary pcs, works like a charm. Also, the start-up takes like 3 seconds.
Audio 5/10:
There is no soundtrack to this game, or so I think, so I'm assessing the background sounds. They are not the main emphasis of the game, and I don't deem it important, but sound can be useful to hear when a riot is about to start etc. The audio is of okay quality, and mainly consists of inmate noises, dogs barking, some sirens in the background, and contruction noise. It's not annoying in any way, but I don't feel it's wonders within indie games either. However, not really important for the game.
Story 9/10:
I wouldn't normally assess story in a simulation game, but the bios and introduction/tutorial is great, mostly humorous and worth the read. I believe most character bios are written by players themselves, and kudos, brilliant work.
Other:
As mentioned, updates are fun, often includes additions to gameplay, some other times; focuses on bug fixes.
As many other simulation games, it lasts, and have replay value.
Conclusion/TL;DR:
It's a great game, and feels finished allready, yet interesting updates are still coming (soon out of early access though).

I was almost put off buying this game because of the recent reviews, but i went ahead anyway as it popped up on sale, and i'm glad i did!

The game is very similar to Rimworld, in that you have 3 "duplicants" to start off with. You meet their needs, such as building a toilet before they start peeing all over the place and creating icky problems.
As you dig through the asteroid/comet you've been dropped into, creating your home, you collect resourses and put those resources to good use.
Build beds, furniture, decorations, computers, create food etc etc.
Research new tech, build better and more resourse preserving devices to help your colony survive for as long as possible.
Every now and again you get the option to add a new "duplicant" to your colony. You can choose to accept, or not. You get a choice of 3, take a look at the stats, their positives, and their negatives, such as a mouth breather wouldn't be the best idea if you are short on oxygen....or if you have beds close together, you might not want to add a loud sleeper that will annoy the hell out of your other "duplicants" who just want to have a good nights sleep ;)

With already owning the card based version and tablet edition for when im out and about, all I can say about boss monster is that it is perfect for beginners and established card game players alike. It is not a complex card game at base level but add in the strategy and thought process to each player competing and it can get as complex as you'd like.
What I like about the PC version is the support for online games, being able to play anyone is amazing. The layout is really decent for the type of game it is, not cluttering when adding more A.I players. The auto attack equation helps, especially if someone new to the game can't outright figure out if they can take on any heroes. The unlocks once they are out will make this game even better than it is. The quality of the images for the cards and the overall colour and detail is really good, and makes the game much more impressive.
There are only a few niggles with the game that I would like to address though. One is the pass and play feature. Although this allows 'couch multiplayer' of sorts, for me personally, would prefer to sit at a table and play this game with physical cards, which only leaves the single player A.I and the online capabilities. Another worry is the sounds. I know they are there for fun and interaction with the cards but they can get a little irritating as they are played after every attack in a room. If they only made the noise once (maybe when they are built) I would be fine with it, but ergo I have had to turn off the sound in the settings. One tiny idea from me would also be to put a total attack number somewhere in your play area, not for me as a player personally who plays the physical game and has to, but for new players who don't want to be adding up their attack total each time.
Overall though, its a perfect game for card beginners to learn what Boss Monster is about and have fun with it with friends, so I highly recommend it for those looking for something new, but if you have the physical edition, its only qualities are what I've said before, the A.I and online. For pass n play multiplayer, I will probably stick with the cards, but when I have no one to play with, the PC edition is where I'm going to go for my Boss Monster urges.
Plus at a price of £5, theres no argument if you dont have the physical game, as this is cheaper than the physical edition, and will allow you to enjoy it as much as me.

This is tough to say, because I love this game.  I own the physical copy, plus the expansion, that I bought from the actual developers at GenCon in 2014.  I even tossed in to KickStarter this digital bad boy, at the Paper and PIxel's level, which has been pretty rad so far.
But this is a NOT so great mobile port for this game.
This is a great game, with brilliant bit art, and fantastic gameplay...
... that is rendered almost unplayable, at times, by the unintuitive UI.
Now, I love mobile games.  I play them all the time. So, using this knowledge, I tried to apply and translate "swiping" and "touching" for pointing, clicking, and scrolling.
This is easy to do.  Until it is not.
Much of this game is slowed down by having to click at the top left of the monitor after viewing cards.  Why is this not easier?  Why can I not, say, left click on a card, then right click on it to make it smaller?
Why are things so slow?  Why do we have animations slowing things down?  Why is the user interface getting in the way?
I think MUCH can be learned from the UI of, say... Magic: The Gathering 2012 though... present.  Or many of the other digital card games available now.
What is annoying is that it is too too easy to miss opportunities to use abilities because... I didn't know what the interface wanted me to do.
It's frustrating to lose games because I had the opportunity to select abilities... but because I didn't know when, or how to draw cards... or where to pull them from, or how to put them down... or when to put them down... or how the game wanted me to put them down... I'll lose a match.
Which is not cool!  Not because I lost.  I lose all the time at stuff.  I've grown quite comfortable with losing.  I'm fine with losing, But I want it to be because I suck at the game.  Not because I'm tripping all over the flippin' UI.
Honestly, I didn't get to play more than 3 games because on the third... the game just... stopped.
I had no idea what it wanted from me.  It was build phase.  I selected a room.  I picked over which room I wanted it to replace.  It was a trap room.  I had an advanced trap room.  Everything looked great.  The game was like, “Sweet dude.  I got this.  You’re good.  Look how I’m ready for you to hit done.”
But there was no “Done”.  No way to advance the turn.
Was I doing it wrong?  I Don't Know!  The game gave me NOTHING.  I tried to put it over another room that was technically invalid, and it discarded the card.   ...which includes a tiny animation and wait... and this happens like... FIVE times as I'm trying to troubleshoot what is going on.  EACH attempt resulting in one of those painful discard animations... which feels like EONS!!!!!
It wasn't actual eons, obviously.  But it felt like it by that point.
This KILLS ME to do but… I can’t recommend this mobile app port right now because… it makes me sad.  And I know it will make other’s sad.  And that’s what reviews are all about.  Opinions.
Hey… support these guys, sure.  They made a great game.
It’s just being murdered by the UI.
Fix the UI.  Make this a Steam friendly game.  Do that… and I’ll fix my recommendation.
Keep up the good work guys.  Feels like this should be an easy fix.

Excellent Pool simulation with superb physics and awesome visuals. The game plays well but the locations lack a little variety. Its certainly worth the purchase and will provide hours of fun and is certainly the best pool game to hit the PC in a long time.
There is a choice of 8 ball and 9 ball play plus various other novel play modes inc speed pool, golf and killer mode.
The control of the game is intuitive and the developers continue to improve the game.
To sum things up I think there was a gap in the market for a good pool game on the PC and this one fills it nicely!

It's kinda tricky to review a Pool game so I will try and break it down into what matters.
Graphics
As you can see in the screenshots the game looks great, it is ported from the Xbox 360 so it will run pretty damn well on almost any computer set up you care to mention and with Anti-alising all the way up it is a very very nice game to look at. The UI is nice and easy to use as well although, whislt the controls have had there names changed. It still asks you to press A, B, Start and Back whenever you want to do something. That is more of a monor niggle though
Gameplay
The Pool on display here is very nice. The balls all act realistically and as far as I can tell things like friction have been modeled very well. In the close up slow-mo shots you get sometimes when a ball is potted you can see that the balls are lifting up and sliding about realistically. The sound design helps to sell this as well, with nice clear sound making it all the more satisfying when the ball drops.
Multiplayer
As far as I can tell the multiplayer for this game is dead. Which is a shame and slightly confusing. I couldn't seem to find any games at all in any mode so unless one of your friends has the game it is most likely gonna be solo play for you.
Overall
Considering The lack of a decent Pool game on PC and the promise of the release of the Trick Shot mode soon I would say this game is well worth picking up

One of the first Space-sim type of games I have found fun in quite a while. The controls/UI wont scare you away and are very functional, and the game feels pretty polished for a new release. While combat only missions are getting slightly repetitive I find the combat itself is very fun if you use manual aim and avoid just getting into a rythym of auto-fire on locked targets. It adds more challenge to the combat and keeps it fresh every encounter trying to dodge incoming fire while positioning yourself correctly to fire your batteries and having to stay on your toes while aiming. I have been seeing a lot of threads calling combat "lackluster" or boring, but every one of them have been people using auto-aim and most likely just flying circles around the enemy ships haha. Of course that would become boring quickly, and the manual aiming is what makes me like this game more than a lot of other space sims that do not even have that option.
On top of the combat there is trading(though not really worth it right now, but patches will surely improve it), mining, and boarding enemy ships to capture and haul back for good cash or to use it yourself. Mercenaries have been fixed in the latest patch as well which I have yet to try so cannot comment on that(allies that fly with you and help in combat which you can control to an extent).
The campaign is pretty basic, but it has a decent story going on and gives you something else to do on the side when you get bored of freelance missions, mining, or trading to get into better ships and better upgrades for each ship.
All in all I am enjoying the game and can't wait to see what else is added down the line(devs have already confirmed they want to add more endgame with station ownership and faction warfare). And to top it all off you can already mod the game and there a few complete revamps already even though the game has just released. Highly recommended if you liked any older space-sims like Freelancer or the like.

This is a fun, engaging "light" strategy / action game. It draws inspiration from both Starfleet Command and EVE online without being nearly as complex as either one. Think of it as
- and you will get the idea.
If you are an experienced gamer in this particular genre you will probably pick up the basics in an hour or so, get a feel for the extent of the content in about 4 to 6 hours playtime - and feel sufficiently masterful after about 10-12 hours.
To enjoy this game you have to patient, enjoy slower paced exploration coupled with quick bursts of fairly asymetrical combat (both in your favor and otherwise) - and be ready to allow for a certain quirkiness that comes from game devs whose native language is not English. On that point the devs are super nice peeps who love to get feedback and talk about how to improve the game on their forums.
Like most games these days, SG2 is evolving. I think what we have now is a solid foundation for many expansions yet to come and I, for one, am looking forward to seeing where it goes from here.
This is definitely a great game for people who, like me, enjoy playing for long stretches at night with groovy techno / trance music in the headphones while watching the beautiful space scenery slip by... without the constant combat of SFC or the massive timesink (and perpetual 2nd class citizen status) of EVE.

Good game, but a bad port. If you want a number score, I would say 3/5.
First, I've played Boss Monster a few times before this electronic version showed up on Kickstarter. I do not own the mobile version.
Let me start by saying I own a Surface Pro 3, a Windows 8.1 tablet. I thought having a digital copy of this would make it fun to play on the go. The problem is the port has some critical bugs they need to fix. Story time...
The major game bug I had is with touch devices, after a while the game loses focus. When you're tapping the screen you're actually clicking behind the game window. When you finally Alt+Tab to the desktop you'll see all these programs open because you've been clicking your shortcuts and items on your desktop. This bug is terrible, and would happen every 3-5 minutes without fail, when not using a mouse. I would have to hit the Windows button a few times to bring up the start menu, then click the program in the task bar, or I would have to hook up a keyboard and forgo the ease of using the Surface as a tablet to recover the game.
This bug seemed to happen in fullscreen, so then I thought "I'll just play in Window mode". Surprise! Here is the first clue this is a cheap port of the mobile version. You get 4 options in the Settings menu. Music volume, sound effect volume, game speed, and fullscreen on/off. "Okay, no real graphic settings, but at least I can make it Windowed" I thought. This brings me to the next major bug. If you have a high resolution screen, like on a Surface Pro 3, the game window is tiny, card text is unreadable. Then you discover you can't resize the window, or make the window take up the full screen. You have two options, tiny unreadable window, or fullscreen. :(
Fine fine... I loaded the game up on my main desktop PC and figured with it's lower resolution screen at least it would be readable in Window mode, and it was! I then figured, "Alright let me play a few games!" That is where I ran into the next issue, again because it is a poor port. This game has minimal Steam features, which tends to be the trend with mobile ports. This means there is no Cloud Saves. To unlock extra Heroes, which is DLC I own, I have to win 40 games... that means I have to win 40 games on each device I own because the save game isn't transferred between my devices or carried over after I reformat. :(
Lastly, some game design choices are weird. When using a touch devices you have to double tap everything to activate, when using a mouse it is a single click. Also the Halt button seems like a waste. There is no reason for the Halt button. The game should show you the 3 buttons, Pass All, Go (Pass Once), and Play Card. If you choose Play Card, then it should pause/halt. There is no reason to have to open a menu 95% of the time just to get to "Pass All". It seems very unnecessary, except as an attempt to save visual space on a mobile device.
Now. Why the thumbs up? It's a fun game, and I hope they fix these issues, it was just released and I trust they'll look into it. Though even things like the "In-App Store" just scream it's a very weak mobile port. I figure once they iron out these bugs with touch devices, and maybe add some graphic settings (at least resolution options or scaling) the game will be perfect for a quick purchase and play on a trip.
Pros:
* The pixel graphics are nice.
* The music is nice.
* Faithful to the card game.
Cons:
* No Steam support (other than trading cards), which means you're save isn't transferred between devices.
* No graphics options
* Poor touch screen/device support
To make this game 5/5, it would have been awesome to have Steam Workshop support, allow people to make custom cards, or at least add new images to existing cards. I feel Steam features, and mods/customizing is locked out to keep the PC/mobile ports the same, and to sell DLC unfortunately. One can dream though...

First things first, I love Boss Monster. It is an amazing game. I helped kick start it and I helped kickstart this port. My negative recomendation is not for the Boss Monster game but for this Steam port.
Anyways, now on to the review of the port. I will try to cover everything that was my initial impression:

The Good:
-Music is nice.

The Bad:
- The UI is extremely unituitive. I managed to destroy one of my rooms without even realizing it (which was hilarious.) It's hard to tell where to go to play certain things and what is going on/what phase you are in.
-  Play moves at glacial speed. One of the fun things about Boss Monster is the speed at which you can knock out a game with a group of buds. A faithful translation of the fantastic card game.
Boss monster is non-collectable card game where you play as the 'boss monster' in a fantasy dungeon.  Inspired by 8 and 16 bit games as well as fantasy RPGs, it has a retro feel with quite a bit of humor thrown in.  You build your dungeon, using treasures in each room to lure hapless "heroes" into your dungeon, only to kill them with a variety of tricky trap rooms, brutal monster rooms, and fiendish spell cards that you can cast.If you take damage from five heroes, you die.  But if you manage to collect 10 heroes souls you win!
Oh, but did I mention there's another boss monster out there with his own dungeon?  Because he's competing with you to lure hapless adventurers into his own dungeon.  Playable against the computer or against friends online, with up to four players (or solo with 3 AI players) the challenge is real.  There's just enough randomness in the cards drawn to balance out the strategy needed to win.
I would suggest people give this game a shot if you've never played the card game.  Because if you have played the card game, you probably already bought this steam version.  It's a monster of a good time.

I'm not afraid to admit: I bought Pool Nation solely on account of its graphics.
Let me elaborate. One of my favorite "sports" games (let's not get into the semantics of whether pool is a sport) of all time has been the original Virtual Pool by Celeris. Since it's been literally years since I played the game, Pool Nation struck all the right chords with me: low price (on sale for $5), great artwork and graphics (ooh, shiny!), and those pangs of nostalgia that I'd been craving.
Pool Nation sports a reasonably good tutorial mode and even teaches you how to pull off expert moves like jump shots, knife-edges, and all sorts of careful maneuvers with curving and banking. And those moves will generally score you loads of style points (which, as far as I can tell, are only useful on the in-game leaderboards - there's no way to spend them, and all the unlockables come from milestones in the Tournament modes).
If I have only one complaint about Pool Nation, it's that the AI suffers from what I like to refer to as "Worms Syndrome"; in short, the AI will alternate between being a complete and utter stooge (like pocketing the cueball) and being freakishly perfect at their shots (I've seen even low-tier opponents like Cousin Merl pull off insane curving bank shots and manage to pot two or more balls in one hit, on occasion).
Of course, this ceases to matter if your intention is playing with friends. This is also a bit of a problem, though, as the online scene for Pool Nation is...well, pretty much nonexistant. You'll pretty much need to talk your friends into buying it if you want to play against anybody other than the AI opponents (or the timer in Endurance Mode). This said, though, given the game's low price, that shouldn't be too hard.
And then, yes, there's the graphics. Everything in this game is really shiny. Not "bloom and HDR" shiny, but nice and reflective and smooth. The pool halls you compete in (there are several!) are lovingly rendered and actually remind me of the city from Mirror's Edge. Then there's the character artwork, which is occasionally hilarious (Cousin Merl and Beef Chillingham both elicited chuckles from my usual Livestream audience).
So, yes, I give Pool Nation my recommendation. There are no crazy arcade elements (you won't see explosions or fancy particle effects); it's pretty much straight pool with a nice coat of gloss and some solid physics.
