They improved the prestige system. First of all I want to mention that this game has a level cap of 55. Everytime you level up you get a token, which you can spend on a perk/weapon/killstreak/equipment. 55 tokens isn't really enough, and it was done on purpose. Now it kind of gives meaning to actually prestige, so that you will be able to test out everything. There are 10 prestiges in the game, when you reach prestige 10, you receive the rest of the gear. Other then that, the game also has MW3's Prestige Shop and Prestige Unlock Tokens. The Prestige Shop gives you 3 options, you can either erase all your stats and set back to level 1(without prestige), add an additional loadout or keep all your tokens. The Prestige Unlock Tokens give you an ability to choose any gear, and permanently unlock it, you get 1 per prestige. The other good thing is that you no longer have your challenges and weapon attachments/camouflage erased when prestiging.Instead they decided to put it in a separate category. Now there is a weapon prestige, allowing you to completely erase all your weapon unlocks on that specific weapon, once you reached weapon's max level.You are allowed to do that 2 times. They reward you with an ability to put your clan name and emblem on that weapon.
One really annoying thing though, are the outdated graphics. This is an AAA title, so I had to mention that. They don't have a low budget, so there is no excuse for them being that outdated.
Conclusion: I give it a below average score. The game is better then MW3. In fact I have to say, if you judge it by it's singleplayer and coop then you may call it the best out of all COD's, but the core of COD for the past 7 years been the multiplayer, and that's what BO2 is lacking of. So I am not really suggesting you to get it, considering that they don't even give it a decent discount.

Usually games based on movies and films are cheap, poorly made and just bad. Mad Max on the other hand, is actually a really good game. Although not perfect, it's probably the best movie-based game I've played since Spiderman first debuted many years ago. Mad Max has amazing visuals and a hefty amount of graphical options, as well as new and refreshing mechanics for vehicle-based gameplay and combat. Foot-combat, reminisent of the Batman games, feels a bit too simple at times, but is still enjoyable. There's a plenty and a variety of fun things to do within the game, including side-quests, customizations and upgrades for Max and your car/truck. There's also a very gritty and realistic sense to the game, especially when random storms come in. Not only do they look really good, but they hurl dangerous amounts of lightning and debris around, both of which you have to either dodge or take shelter from. That, along with the limited food and water supply you have to keep an eye out for to replenish your health and the limited amount of fuel for your vehicle, really gives a survival aspect that I did not expect from a game such as this, yet it's also not as intense to where you're not enjoying the game when you do have to find these necessities.
Again, the game is really good and quite fun, but it is not perfect. My main gripes are that there are certain times where the A.I. could be better. Often I would find myself trying to reason with NPC's, telling them they could have realized or done something a lot sooner than they had. Also, Max himself seems to forget where his enemies are occasionally when in foot-combat, as he will face the opposite way and punch/kick air for a few seconds. There are certain areas were Max can climb or vault on, which are usually marked with yellow paint, but there are also other areas that are much smaller than the things he climbs that are not marked, yet for some reason he still can't climb them. There are also times where I wish there were some sort of options for the HUD, because sometimes I'm left wanting to take away some of the HUD, or at least shoving it all closer to the edges of the screen. This may only be a problem for resolutions above 1080p though. There are a few mission related bugs, for instance, the dog seems to sometimes think mines are buried at locations where you already had defused them. After Death Runs (vehicle-based challanges), the game sometimes gets confused as to whether you lost the Death Run or died, which may become frustrating at times. Some of the larger textures could have been better, such as the night sky and the sludge pits, but all other textures seemed relatively great. Also, corpses tend to disappear too early, the game should at least wait until the player leaves the area.
All in all, Mad Max runs very well, plays very well and is just downright solid and fun, especially for a movie game, and is also a worthy installment to the Mad Max storyline and a great follow-up to Mad Max: Fury Road.

Mad Max, game open world ini cocok banget buat lo semua yang suka dengan game adventure ditambah aksi-aksi fighting moves-nya yang brutal abis. Fitur fast travel khas open world game bakal membantu banget kalo lagi males nyetir atau mau kabur dari kejaran musuh. Pemandangan jalan tandus dan gurun ga seburuk yang lo bayangkan, pengaturan cahaya di game ini dan weather effect-nya keren abis. Badai gurun nampak realistis, petir yang menyambar saat badai keliatan jelas dan nyata, begitu juga dengan percikan dan nyala api dari setiap benda yang meledak. Karakter juga audio cukup bagus dan story-nya juga ga kalah seru dengan movie-nya game ini.
Di beberapa bagian game ini bisa bikin lo jenuh, beberapa side quest dan looting scrap bisa agak membosankan kalo terus berulang. Boss battle di sini juga bisa dibilang repetitif, dari mulai tampilan Boss/Top Dog-nya yang cuma beda warna sampai cara bertarungnya yang lo pasti cepet banget hapal setiap pergerakan serangannya. Karena serangan yang lambat dan mudah dihindari, bikin boss battle di game ini kurang menantang. Pergerakan karakter Max juga ada sisi negatif khususnya saat kita lompat, hanya tempat-tempat rendah dan tertentu saja yang bisa dilompati atau dipanjat.
Grafik yang bagus cukup ringan walaupun dengan spec PC yang tidak terlalu powerful. Kisaran waktu tamat game ini 15 jam waktu main dan untuk para completionist atau achievement hunter, dalam waktu 70+ jam semua achievement bisa lo dapetin.

This game, wow. It is eating away at my soul here. Like I need to sacrifice another small vessel for creds so I can sleep again.
I bought this game cause I had a gut feeling it was what I needed in a game right now. Yeah sure there are others like it, but I just wanted singleplayer and something really solid and fun. An man was I in for a treat! I had no idea I could enjoy a game so much again, like back in the day with all the old systems around and gramps was trying to figure out why the TV is calling him.
So far the story has been very engaging with some smug and unsavory characters, not to mention a bunch of stuff to do on the way. Clearing asteroid fields for some spare loot to fill that cargo hold, capturing enemy ships to either sell or dock for your own collection. Beaming aboard your crew to steal stuff for you on a old mining field or enemy ship in battle to turn the tide an steal it for yourself, you will have to tractor beam it the whole way at impulse speeds to the nearest planet or station of course, who wants to do anything the easy way any way? Psssh.
You have your classic worm holes you can use to travel or them good ole relays for cash, but who wants to waste money?
Also you will run into random slipstreams in which you can use to traverse.. well the verse, by steering your ship properly through it. Be warned about worm holes though you can loose people, but don't worry you can get more red shirts at the nearest docking bay :D.
Even combat is savvy. Tell your people to fire at will, take the helm do it yourself or root all power to engines as the words of Firefly's Jane "Let's Moon'm" cascades from your lips like lavander and oats. Be a commander, be THE commander. Hire merc ships to roll in your space posse, have a fleet of some bad to the bone misunderstood ship captains looking for redemption and love among the stars. You can of course also customize your ships colors and a few decals, but the real bread n' butter is the all the parts you can fit the ships with. An there is a lot of parts ranging from pulsar cannons to rail guns.
You are not constrained in anyway wanna be that scruffy looking nerf herder? You can! Got that Serenity Smuggling Fever? This game has the cure my friend! Wanna travel across space corralling convicts like Cowboy Bebop? See you space cowboy, I'll be chilling with Jet. Wanna make enemies of a gang Outlaw Star Style? Look no further time to pop that space cherry Gene Starwind! Need to feel like you're back in Star Fleet Academy with Kirk? Picard? Riker? Janeway? Tuvok? Classes start as soon as you hit the buy button cadet! An tell Neelix I sent ya ;D.
What is also great is that the devs have been very responsive and helpful working with the community to solve issues, active devs have really made this product shine and continues to better. I do hope you get the game and enjoy as much as I am.
In my conclusion yes I recommend this amazing game, I have spent the last few years just really yearning for something, but sure what exactly. When I saw this I knew my sacrifice to the Game Satan had finally been heard. The graphics are solid and just breathtaking, the gameplay is as smooth as Bruce Willis's bald spot in The 5th Element. An steam workshop also? All I can say is beam me up Scotty, we can do it Captain this time we have the power.

But there it stayed in early access for aaaages, eventually I bought a copy and enjoyed the little it had to offer but now it finally has it's full release there is just so little in the way of 'finished product' here.
Everything feels rushed, the space combat is a little clunky but holds up well enough however the interactions in the game aren't even as detailed as Freelancer, a game that was released back in 2003 has more fine detail than Starport Gemini 2?
When you 'dock' at a station you press a button and 'pop', you are 'docked' with a static Azimov-style background and a menu, that's it. No animation, no ship descending from the clouds or going into a station, just a menu.
The NPC dialogues are also static little windows in the corner of the screen, which is ok but for a game that has languished in Early access for so long I would have expected a little more in the way of 'polish'.
As far as I can tell the graphics options still haven't all been implemented and some options are just greyed out.
The campaign mode feels entirely tacked-on last minute and isn't engaging in the least. I know this last thing is going to sound silly but it really is something that breaks the immersion of a space sim and that's the lack of a cockpit-view, the 'X' franchise made this same mistake reducing the interface to little more than a huge pile of menus. This is 2014, this game 'should' be a lot better.
Save your money for Elite Dangerous or Star Citizen, this game is just embarrasing.

This is a very simple and basic space tactical simulation...
You control only 1 ship and you move around in a square board in 2D tactial fashion.
There are 21 stages and all with minimum story and progression through this entire thing..
You can either exit though space portal each map quickly or fight until there are no reinforcment for every stage before moving on.
Your ship gain EXP and you level up for 1 skill point each level which you can spend on various improvment.
Even if you die. Your ship's level/EXP and already gained skills stays..You can customize your already gained skill every time under the game menu.
There are about 6 different equipment slot that each dedicate for different equipment you get by killing/looting from enemy ships you destoried. You can equip more equipment that use a differet equipment slot(like an extra weapon using scaner slot) by skills under the game menu.
Music is basic mono with no surpises and repetitive. Sound Effect is decent. Graphic is sub par unity engine. Game is easy to learn and easy to master.(just gota figure out when and where to direct energy from shield to weapon/engine).
Only challange you will have is last level.(or level 2 if u don't move away from the enemy destoryer.
The ending is not very satisfactory.
For a game that nearly don't cost anything at all.. it's would be a basic learning experience for the developer and offer enough enjoyment and thinking for a few hours only.
Achivements are quite easy to get though out the game and they are quite hard to miss even...
A get a few solid hours of enjoyment and worth the 1 dollar I send for this.. Nothing more.. nothing less.
6.5/10 is my final rating for this dollar indie game.

Rise of the Triad: Dark War is a classic FPS that was released in 1995. It's a Wolf3D-like engine game. A very heavily modified one though. Choose one of the fie characters and kill everything while running real fast.
Now, how was Steam version handled? Pretty nice. It runs on a good DosBox software, all configured properly and with working Steam overlay. You can configure game to use standard WASD and mouse too.
When you launch the game, you will get to choose one of the three games. Dark War is what you should choose, as this is the full version of a game.
Hunt Begins is a shareware version of a game. A Deluxe Shareware version, which came with few additional levels. Yes, somebody made Deluxe Shareware back then. It has exclusive levels, so it's worth playing. The only shame is that it has Full Version's ending instead of shareware one. Try not to spoil yourself there.
Extreme ROTT is extremely extreme expansion pack for ROTT, which is extremely crazy, insane, sick maniac. It adds no new elements like music or gameplay, instead it's more like a hack that replaces levels with it's own. Yea, ending is same, bosses are same. It's just that levels are so cheap and unfair, it's unbelivably. Watch review on YouTube, I hope it will make you not to want to even touch this one.
If you do however going to play Extreme, use Thi Barrett, the only char that can beat jumping puzzle in one of the levels. Also, create save at the beggining of each level in case you get stuck while trying to beat them. Then enjoy your savescumming feature presentation.
Original game also supported multiplayer. And quite gloriuosly, with lots of players and many many game modes. But I doubt that you can make it run easily nowdays, probably due to using outdated technology. Or whatever. I didn't even try much, just know that it sure will not be so easy or straightforward. Maybe it doesn't even work. Get this game for single-player anyway.
And well, it's quite awesome. To be honest, my first impression was negative one. I picked Lorelei Ni character, who is fast but is very fragile compared to other character, and picked the third skill out of four, which is actually "hard", and then I was quickly mashed up by bullets. You see, game's majority of enemies use unadvoidable hitscan attacks. Bullets, you know. That's something what should never be dangerous too much, or else it will become more cover-based. I didn't like it back then.
Morale of story: Don't pick Lorelei. And stay on Normal difficulty.
So, yes, you can pick any one of the five characters. Their main differences are stats that are: Speed, Accuracy and Health. Speed isn't much of use there due to often use of hitscan. Everybody aside from Lorelei has high Accuracy, she just has Very High. Ultimately, health it what matters there. Consult with manual to see stats for yourself. Also, should be noted that there is one character who is superior to another with no downsides. So yea, it's not all too clever. The other differences are occasional voice and camera height.
The way how game looks will immmeditly catch your attention. Not only because those digitized nazi-like enemies look awesome and have character to them. And grayish enviroments, with gothic style can be seen slightly in them. But you will notice just how far they were pushing modified Wolfenstein 3D engine. Moving walls, tall rooms, using platforms objects to give verticality to the gameplay. It's quite a joy.
Also helps that it has awesome Midi music to it. One of the best. You will find memoriable tune for sure. There is even piano music that sounds castlevania-worthy. Seriously.
As for gameplay, you run around mazes and shoot things down. And avoiding traps. Developers weren't afraid to be ridiculous crazy and went ahead, putting every thing they belived were cool. There are even things that make you bounce off the floor high into air. And power-ups that I shall not spoil.
Weapon selection is interesting. And silly. You start with single pistol, then can get second pistol and machine gun. Yes, those are direct updates. With infinite ammo.  And then you have rocket launchers of different types, some more devastating than others. So, yes, it will be ludicrous gibs fun time for you there. Rocket Launchers aren't the only weapons, but I told you nothing, okay?
The silly thing is how it handles player's weapon equipment. For some reason, you can keep pistols and machine gun, they don't replace each other, even though they are direct upgrades to each other. On other hand, you can only hold one rocket launcher. You would think that it should be another way around. Or just let machine gun replace pistols. But oh well.
Maps are huge and mazey. Will make you go around, flipping switch and finding keys. And finding hidden floorplates, that are hard to see and sometimes mandatory. Not exactly nice thing. Actually, it becomes negative, as on Episode 2 there is one huge outdoor level, that has impressive huge size. And it would be awesome, if it didn't made you run around, finding switches in every corner and inspecting map verrry carefully in search for touchplates. Seriously, I found secret exit there first.
Shooting should be good. After all, you got good basic weapon with infinite ammo and rocket launcher to blow things up. And it's true, blowing people up is fun. They also easily get locked in hitstate when shot by machine gun, so one on one encounter is never a problem, it's always crowds. Episode 1 has only cannon fodder, that yell cliche things at you. Episode 2 introduces a really tough enemy that has enough health to requrie few hits from rocket launcher. It makes better use of rocket launchers for once, but shooting him down when out of rockets gets tedious. Episode 3 introduces robots that can be killed with just rocket. But they are quite passive patrollers, so it's still good variety.
But Episode 4, the last one, is where game goes down. It exclusively uses tough monks enemies. And they are tough. Way too tough. They are also boring and tedious. Just shooting them down with machine gun will take what feels like a minute. And there is only two of them, melee and slow one and the one which shoots fireballs. Still can be locked in painstate by machine gun. Yea. All tedious.
But hey, game also has bosses. More or less good ones. That walk around and shoot things at you and use other gimmicks. So yes, more or less proper ones. Third episode boss is known to be the hardest thign in the game. All while Episode 4 boss is most stupid one. The first part of 4th boss is bad, it just has you waiting for him run out of energy for what feels like 10 minutes. The latter part is stupid in good way though.
So, ROTT is a mix between good and bad. Amazing ideas, trying to push Wolfenstein-era engine to the maximum, but has occasional stupid or tedious things. And it's still one of those things where you get rained by hitscan, not avoiding projectiles as much. Navigating around traps though. Try it. It's probably more positive than negative. Yes, it is.

I do not like Rogue Legacy. It makes me sad inside. I got it on sale for when it was extraordinarily cheap and it still felt like a ripoff. I understand that people really like this game, and I can see why people like the concept- every time you die (which will be a lot, the game is bloody hard), you get a new character with a "special ability". The novelty of these wears off very quickly and very easily becomes a boring waste of what could have been a good run. Also I don't know if it's just me, but the game crashes lots.
Other than that I do really like the art style.

First and foremost a controller of some kind is pretty much mandatory unless you really enjoy masochism.
Rogue Legacy is a pretty average rogue-lite overall if you only play through the game's "story" (which should occupy you for about 6-8 hours) without aiming for 100% however should you go for 100% the game devolves into a rather boring grindfest gated by multiple layers of RNG and then a group of super bosses who are hard for all the wrong reasons.
Character "Creation": Rogue Legacy revolves around adventuring through a castle until you die and one of your descendants takes over were you left off.
Of course each descendant is a little different from the last in terms of their class, traits, and spell. There are 10 classes in Rogue Legacy (1 of which is your reward for defeating the Remix Bosses so you won't see it in regular gameplay) which seems like a nice variety for a rogue-lite however there are classes that feel very similar to each other. In addition the line that seperates the classes blurs the more you upgrade your castle since these upgrades apply to all your descendants and there is nothing like a reset/respec in the game. Then there are 37 traits and each descendant can up to 3 traits. These traits range from the good, like being able to see the location of every enemy in each room to you enter, to the bad, your whole screen is flipped upside down, to the mundane, your character farts occasionally when you jump or dash. My personal breakdown of the traits are as follows:
Good: 11
Bad: 11
Mundane: 15 (included in here are also traits that either might have no effect (e.g. Ambilevous) or that can be good or bad (e.g. Dextrocardia))
Overall the way you choose your character is unique and is one of the main draws of Rogue Legacy but with there being only one way to re-roll characters which only comes later on in the game you might find yourself becoming frustrated because you can't choose spelunker when you start to grind for runes/blueprints or you can't choose a specific class to take on a boss. Still it is a unique concept that encourages the player to try classes they might otherwise shy away from.
Gameplay: The game controls well though the way that it handles moving back while attacking may take a while to get used to. Exploring the different areas of the castle is fun and there is a nice variety of room layouts. The fairy chest challenge rooms can be fun though many rely on you having a specific rune set up or character trait. The runes that you get from these fairy chests can grant you abilities such as extra jumps or dashes (you can also get these from armour pieces later on in the game) but the variety is not large enough to constitute many different play-styles as the mobility runes are usually too good to give up on unless you're grinding in which case you're using bounty/curse runes anyway. The armour/weapon selection is average, there are a few sets that have you take a dip in one stat for a big increase in another but these don't come till much later in the game and it is entirely possible to  go through the game without ever seeing them.
Earlier on I said that the game becomes a grindfest when going for 100% and that's because of the blueprint/rune hunt. The most optimal class is obviously the spelunker because you can see the location of fairy chest rooms/treasure chests. However you won't always get the spelunker class in your descendant menu which can be a ballache as you have to make the choice of whether you suicide and roll the dice again or trudge on with the character you got. Then fairy chest challenge RNG comes in effect (as mentioned above). Then when going for blueprints you'll eventually only be able to get them by either defeating mini-bosses or getting a calypso's compass from a spiritual shrine (more RNG) then not dying before you get to the secret room that the compass leads you to.
The enemies of Rogue Legacy are interesting between the eyes that will shoot at you from anywhere in the room to painting mimics and skeltal heads that will float through walls to get to you each enemy "tree" behaves differently from each other however that leads onto my next point: the enemy variety in Rogue Legacy is sadly lacking with many of the enemies you find in the later areas simply being re-skins of previous enemies but with more health + damage/projectiles. Even the mini-bosses are only overly strong versions of regular enemies. In addition to this Rogue Legacy is rather fond of projectile throwers so expect to take more than 1 fireball to the face over the course of the game. The bosses are rather fun and each of them plays different from each other though there are arguments to be made that there is a difficulty spike between the 1st and 2nd (intended) bosses.
Presentation: The designs of the enemies and areas are all very slick and are a pleasure to look. The Darkness area in particular really hit the mark in feeling like a dank dungeon where you'd find the hardest of the hard of enemies and skeletons are always a plus.
Music: The music is fine, nothing really too special though certain themes such as the main theme, Ponce de Leon's theme and the final boss' theme all hit the mark and are my personal favourites of the OST. The areas themes are all also very catchy but there's only so many hours that you can listen to them before you get sick of 'em.
*SPOILERS FOR THE REMIX BOSSES AHEAD*
The remix bosses are possibly the biggest gripe I have with going for 100%. I love a challenge in a game but only when RNG doesn't play a major factor. Sadly Neo Khidr and Alexander IV can bone you over with RNG. Neo Khidr only has 3 moves but when 1 of them is a (seemingly) pure RNG fest of projectile spam it takes away from your loss and makes it feel cheap. Then Alexander IV's furies add an unnecessary sprinkle of RNG into an already difficult fight especially when Alexander's great balls of fire mask the furies and their projectiles. Ponce de Freon is a slog of a fight with the only thing changed is the platforms and how long the fireballs stay around for. Herodotus is cool though.
*SPOILER END*
TLDR: Rogue Legacy is worth it's price especially if you're a fan of the rogue-lite formula and double especially if you like a game that you can just play music over and mindlessly grind gold for an hour or 2 to upgrade your castle (though this isn't necessary in order to beat the game). However if you're a completionist then be forewarned that this game will frustrate you more than once with deaths against bosses that might not feel fair.

I wouldn't recommend the game. I found this game to be impossibly difficult for a number of reasons, and thus was only actually able to have fun when I used Cheat Engine, to cheat. Yup... Anyway, the reasons why I didn't find the game doable was:
1. Controls = I don't have a game controller, so I had to play with mouse and keyboard. Well, the game refuses to use my mouse, so had to manually edit the keys to have both hands on the keyboard. Very awkward and I constantly hit the wrong key by accident; I've played other platformer type games that suggest controller, but I played them with mouse and keyboard just fine, but not here. Also, I had a dastardly time pulling off the downward jab attack to activate the platformers and thus frequently lost characters by missing the timing and landing on a spike and dying.
2. Platforming = I found the platforming aspects almost always impossible to do. I'm not a very good platformer in general, and this game frequently needs pixel perfect jumping to avoid hitting spikes or to avoid getting hit by enemies. Also, getting hit by enemies causes knockback, which further causes problems on very narrow edges. But the most irritating part of it all was the platforms that extend for 3 seconds, tops. When you are struggling with the controls, are constantly missing your pixel perfect jump, getting hit all the time and you have these platforms... you end up dead a lot of times, which isn't fun.
3. Enemies = Enemies scale in difficulty far too fast, and as a mage, an enemy can 3 hit kill you, but without regenerating mana, you run out of mana very quickly with spells and have to get into melee combat. And as the controls are finicky, melee combat is a real chore to do.
Perhaps if I had a game controller my experience might be different. Maybe; I doubt it. So buyer beware... This game is far harder than most roguelikes on the market and without a controller, you likely wouldn't succeed at all... unless you do like me and cheat. I'll keep playing it with my cheats, and likely keep enjoying it; wish I didn't have to play with cheats though, as there is a real gem of a game here... if you can progress and enjoy it. I couldn't, without cheating.

Been planning on buying this game for several months before spending $20 on it, and boy was waiting worth it, as I got to try it during a free to play weekend. At first my friend and I couldn't get an online private match to work, but it turns out you need at least 4 people to even be able to do a private match. So if you are with just one or two other friends you would have to join the online games with strangers, which, in all honesty, can make the game more fun. The servers are otherwise fantastic. Only disconnects that happened to me and my friends were either us standing around for too long or their Internet personally cutting out. I do live on the US East Coast towards the north, for reference, just in case the servers do not work out for you.
However, we felt the map selection was boring. I did do several rounds of local multiplayer and got to play two maps that were no longer there just the next day (those maps were Wheel and Girders, one was a Ferris Wheel and the other was a small construction site. They were very enjoyable to play but I couldn't even play them with any of my friends because they were gone the day they installed it)
The game's controls can be very annoying to some. I got used to them very quickly, but one of my friends who plays tons of games that require super precise timing on button presses found that the delayed jump and other movements were very annoying and hard to work with. The controls also take a while to get the hang of, nevertheless while you're being dominated by others online.
All in all, I don't recommend buying this right now. It is still in Early Access, so I do hope that a much bigger selection of maps or even a Workshop that has community-made maps, is added so that the fun we had for a few hours can last a while. The price tag is definitely not worth it as of right now, as there are many better multiplayer games that you can get multiple copies of for $20. If you're reading this in the day or days after this review is posted, I feel like the $13.39 price tag can be a good value for some, including myself.
Going to give this game a "Not Recommended" for right now, but will make sure to come back to this game when it is out of Early Access as it does have tons of potential.

You think of a lot of Star Wars games and you're probably thinking of Republic Commando, Battlefront, Knights of The Old Republic and so on. This is the game that I think everyone, even if you're not a fan of Star Wars, should play it. As mentioned in PCGamer, it makes the lightsabers feel like sabers rather than a neon stick with high damage. These lightsabers are rods of superheated plasma, and my god does it let you know that. Stand close enough to a wall, and where your saber would clip through the wall, it cuts it, leaving a burning trail through the wall. If it rains, the water hisses and makes steam. These babies are also one or two hit kills too - you can chop off your enemies limbs with finesse if you're fast enough.
There is absolutely nothing stopping you from never using a gun (apart from one mission where you are captured), and the sabers themselves also have a vareity of unique moves depending on which saber you can choose. Yes, you can customise your saber. Colour, hilt and type. Want Darth Maul's red saber staff? You can choose red as your colour in MP (or if you want, pick an aggressive shade of orange. The purple is also known for striking fear into the hearts of your enemies). You can also customise your character. In fact, the only solid thing is your name, the helpfully ambigous Jaden Korr. Your race, gender and clothing is up to you. Also the female player is voiced buy Jennifer Hale, otherwise known as female Shepard.
The multiplayer community is also somewhat active, but remember, if you're a beginner to the saber (even if you've finished the game) there is always that one guy who is just better than you. It can be aggravating, but get some friends, and it's amazing.
This game is amazing, the only game currently that a wookie can wield a lightsaber. 'Nuff said.

I normally don't write reviews. I enjoy games for myself and that's it. I've been playing Hitman and is a fan of the series since Hitman 2: Silent Assassin. But seeing all these negative reviews for what I feel is THE BEST HITMAN GAME to date is really annoying.
#1) Technical issues: You play on PC, get your♥♥♥♥♥♥together and act like it. Sure, sometimes there are real technical challenges with PC games (when the Dev's mess up). MOST of the time you read the stream forums, are just people who lack computer knowledge to self troubleshoot. Yes, your firewall can make you disconnect. Yes, sometimes you need administrator rights. Yes, sometimes your page caching is too high/too low. Yes, you need to update your drivers from time to time. Yes, you need to turn off Vent, TS3, Skype, iTunes, or whatever other♥♥♥♥♥♥you have open to run any high resource program (eg. any modern video game.) for it to run and load smoothly. And if your PC JUST fit the MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS, YOURE GONNA NEED TO OPTIMIZE IT YOUR SELF AND END UP RUNNING EVERYTHING ON LOW. If you fit the RECOMMENDED REQUIREMENTS, YOURE GONNA NEED TO OPTIMIZE IT YOURSELF AND MAYYYYBE RUN IT ON MEDIUM WITH CERTAIN THINGS TURNED OFF. ITLL LOOK GOOD, BUT DONT EXPECT MAX SETTINGS WITH YOUR 2011 MEDIUM RANGE CARD. The game is pretty guaranteed if you had a CLEAN INSTALL of windows with recommended spects and updated drivers to work. Because there is such a wide hardware base for PC, youre gonna run in to issues sometimes and its up to the enduser to troubleshoot, or ask for help. Instead of whinning to the devs saying its poor software optimization and programming. Whinning like a child online doesn't help your case. Write full sentences and quit using so many curse words. All that porn you've downloaded, the adware you have on your PC, and the always on background routines are gonna slow down your PC,
I've had 0 technical issues. No crashes, no game breaking bugs, no graphical hic-ups. Really rock solid technically speaking. If you do have issues, google is your friend. Ask a tech-y friend. Ask reasonable questions on a forum that is NOT filled with kiddies (I do NOT recommend the steam forums. Maybe go on reddit and word your question/problem really reasonablly, people tend to respond better). Did you know that for optimal PC health, it's recommended to format your OS once a year? When was the last time you cleaned out your PC?
If you act like a child and want instant gratification and lack problem solving skills, do us all a favor and get on consoles.
#2) Always online: Yes, this game drops if you lose your connection. That is an issue and I'm SURE THEY'RE LOOKING TO FIX IT. That is the big downside to this game currently. HOWEVER, there is a contracts mode that is shared online, there is a constant data stream for leaderboards, there is also your Square Enix Account link, there is also achievements and such for syncing with your account. So yeah, it needs a connection. Contracts mode is a feature in the game that REQUIRES INTERNET. Youre missing on a whole feature if youre offline. (I get this isnt an MMO, im using a hyperbole) It's like asking an MMO to play it in your own world in single player. This game also has an OFFLINE MODE. Use it if you have a poor connection or dont have internet. This isn't a game like The Division where you NEED a connection to get in. It runs off servers as opposed to the client.
#3) Gameplay: If you've never played a Hitman game, there has never been a better time to start. Under $20 bucks for the intro, it's a steal of a price. The tutorial is really easy to get in to, great huge sandbox map in Paris. Loads of replayability in terms of sandbox play and online contracts mode. Tons to unlock and discover. I've only played Showstopper twice and each time I play it, it gets more fun. The world is just FILLED with so much stuff to kill with and it's just fun standing around listening to conversations. The details are amazing. The iconic dark humor of the Hitman franchise is littered around the map. Great graphics, great sound design, great writing of witty and satiricle dialogue, and so many options to kill with! You can get seriously creative. For under $20, there really isnt a reason to not try it.
If you're a long time fan, this is it. THE Hitman experience. Think Blood Money, but on tons of steroids of steroids made the game more fun. It takes all the positive out of Blood Money and Absolution (Sandbox maps, modern graphics, detailed worlds, OPTIONS! LOTS OF OPTIONS TO KILL AND EXPLORE AND TO BE PLEASANTLY SURPRISED BY, and the ever so awesome, Contracts Mode). Personally, I dished out the Full Experience because as a long time Hitman fan, this is the Hitman game I've been waiting for. I enjoyed absolution, but Blood Money is the pinnacle, and this dials up that to a whole new level. I know the new maps and upcoming challenges are worth it. Think of this as an investment if you're a long time fan. Even if you are a long time fan but is on the fence, try the intro pack. its like under $20. A steal of a bargain.
#4) Finally: thank you for reading. As of the current climate, Steam Reviews and Steam Forums are not a good place to get a good judgement on the game. Hope you found this review helpful, stranger!

Gameplay:Rogue Legacy is simple, it's a randomly generated 2D action game. You have very simple combat, and platforming abilities. The main gameplay loop is collecting as much gold as possible before your inevitable death, and then upgrading your subsequent characters. It's initially fun, but starts to feel like work, especially if you're doing multiple run throughs and aren't able to scrounge enough gold to collect something.
Presentation: Graphically it's quite nice. There are minor variances to your characters which can be fun. The enemies do fall into recolour territory and there is a lot of asset reuse for being procedurally generated. The soundtrack is forgettable, but most of the in game sounds are quite satisfying.
Difficulty: Rogue Legacy has an extreme difficulty spike. Initially you are incredibly weak. Pathetically weak. Then after numerous attempts, you reach a point where you're capable of surviving long enough to fight the bosses reasonably.
Length: A recent completed playthrough was just over 8 hours with a brief foray into New Game+. A playthrough at release getting 100% compeltion was casually completed in just over 24 hours. There's a good chunk of game here if you're looking for 100%, but whether or not you like the game will be apparent within the first hour.
Final Verdict: Rogue Legacy isn't a bad game, but it's gameplay loop is only going to appeal to a certain set of players. For fans of rogue-likes, they'll probably dislike the progression system and emphasis on success through death. For casual players, they may be put off by the initial difficulty spike.

All in all, though, PA is a fairly solid sim with simple but high-contrast graphics (and the install is tiny), a fair amount of things to consider, and probably not enough guidance on some of the details of some key items / buildings, but you knew coming into a game like this you'd be going to take a few Mulligans before you get the basics down.
The tutorial does a decent job of showing you the controls and most of the daily flow of the prison, but not really enough about how to GET it there (but then, that's the point, right?); You get a glimpse somewhere in the middle of a running small prison's 'day in the life', and from there can start a prison of your very own.
You start out with a basic SimCity toolset, and over time earn upgrades, new staff, new abilities and structures as you service more and more inmates and deal with the logistics issues that come along with it.  The game does a good job of automatically taking care of most of the lower-end micromanagement (e.g. a prisoner in a holding cell is enough of a security risk to warrant their own cell; once you build one and it becomes available, a guard will take a suitable prisoner to that cell to be housed from there).  However, your idle staff will float around if they don't have a task to work on, so to optimize efficiency, you not only have to plan and design your buildings effectively, but manually place staff at key locations to squeeze every dollar you can.
There's a wealth of wiki information online, and you WILL have questions such as the details between door types, some of the key requirements of spacing, etc.  There's a planning tool in-game to alleviate some of this, that allows you to place buildings and objects in a nonbinding mode to set markers for later builds.
Prisoners will fight if their needs aren't being met, or security is lax, delivery trucks will back up if you don't have enough worker staff or storage space, the canteen food trays will pile up if not enough cooks are present to wash them between meals, etc, so there are plenty of little things you have to get right, within your budget limitations, but then there's a sandbox mode so you can optionally build whatever you want without sacrifices.
Overall, a sim that feels right; giving you enough things to worry about, but not more than you can handle even without stopping the timer (save for those first few runthroughs).  If you wanted fancier icons, more scenarios or other mods, this  is a Workshop-enabled title, and there are plenty of resources in the community to extend replayability.  This game will run on practically any modern PC with ~150MB of space, so at the right price, a worthwhile companion until OitNB Season 4 comes out ;)

I paid $0.15 for $0.21 worth of cards, and was mildly interested because it was a turn-based strategy.
It actually turned out to be a decent game. The goal is to find a new homeworld in enemy territory and each level throws a wave of enemies at you. You can choose to complete the objective or just find the exit and escape to the next level.  On the way you find equipment for your ship and earn experience to improve your base abilities.  Your abilities carry over to future games, so you should do better with each attempt.
There are a few things I'd love to see improved:
1. The enemies have terrible pathing.  They always take the most direct route to you unless blocked by another ship. This means they won't surround you when they should.  To be fair, some levels have so many enemies that if you were surrounded, you wouldn't last long.
2.  When you level up you actually have to quit the game, return to the main menu, and select a new ability, then restart. This is unnecessary.  It would be nice if it let me pick a new ability before continuing with the next level.
3. The difficulty ramped up quickly, or at least the instructions for the bomber level weren't explicit enough.  After having only a mild challenge, I was suddenly killed in one hit.

This is an interesting little space roguelike made in a free version of unity.  It has promise, but may not be worth your time.
Pros:
Cheap.  At the time of purchase this only cost 15 cents.
Decent help.  The help screens if you flip through them do a pretty good job of explaining how to play.  Some of the art assets are OK.
Cons:
This is a very rough around the edges product.  There is a lot of polish missing.
Small spelling errors throughout ("sacrifise", "3 enemies is approaching", etc.)
Gameplay itself is both easy and boring, and yet also tedious.  You start off slow and will be hitting the end turn button a lot.
The map does not scroll with you which gets annoying as soon as you can move faster.
The art is pretty bad in many cases.
The font is too large.  The whole game feels designed for a phone and not for a PC.
The later gear does not have clear descriptions, and there are no pop-up or context menus on anything.  This means that figuring out what new gear does is a matter of trial and error.  Now you CAN flip gear back and forth for free, so this helps.  Sometimes I noticed no difference from equipping a new piece of gear.
A story is told, but you have no input, and I found myself quickly skipping past the screens.
Needing to quit a level and "lose all progress" to spend skill points quickly gets annoying.
At the end of the day it isn't bad for someone's first try at a game.  This is not the sort of project that should be sold, unless you like paying for someone else to learn game design.  The game is boring, easy and tedious with poor artwork.  It feels like a school project.

I had my doubts walking into this.  25$ was pretty steep for an EA game, and I don't remember having particularly high enjoyment values out of a management game like this one.  All I could think was:  "This is going to be really simple, isn't it?"
WRONG.
The simplicity of the visual artstyle is very disarming, and leads you into a false sense of confidence, for underneath lies a complicated cluster♥♥♥♥ of depthful mechanics.
A good example is the gas system.  Make sure there's oxygen or you're dead.  Simple, right?
WRONG.
You have to account for gas pressure, the spread and blockage of oxygen being able to spread due to harmful gasses, infectous gasses, gas density, vaccums, even
.
Ok, no big deal, you can learn, right?  Just filter out all the bad stuff, and keep the good stuff pumping in.  Easy as pie...  Right?
WRONG.
You need electricity to keep the oxygen flowing, to get electricity you need resources, to get resources you need able duplicants, to get able duplicants you need to keep them from stressing, to keep them from stressing they need decorations, to get decorations you need resources, to get resources you need able duplicants, to get able duplicants you need edible foo--
And this is just dipping your feet into the pool of mechanics, there's a lot more to be discovered here.  However, one of my
things about this game is the lack of RNG.
Other than spawning the world and adding in new duplicants, there is almost no RNG to be found here.  If your colony's dying of suffocation, that's not the game creating a special event that removes x% of oxygen in the area.  Your colony is suffocating/starving/overheating/freezing/dying because at some point in the past,
Remember that block you dug out under that water pool?  Well guess what?  The water escaped through the cracks and now everyone is drowning!
If you've been looking for a management game that is punishingly difficult while also being entirely fair, buy it.  If you've been looking for a management game that has more than just happy/food/tempurature management, buy it.  If you love learning through trial and error, buy it.
The only reason why I'm not giving it a 10/10 is that it's been a while since the last major content update (plenty of hotfixes, don't worry) and it is admittedly quite barebones in some areas of gameplay.  Extremely well done mechanics, but a small lack of actual content.
Get this game, seriously.

Updated review as of October 1st.
First impressions: Broken. With a lot of potential.
Secondary impressions: It's an acquired taste. It does grow on you. But it's lopsided. Strong gameplay props up a (very) weak campaign.
Initial review:
This game may be out of early access, but do not be fooled. This is NOT a finished product. Not even close. It is sorely lacking in decent voice acting, and the campaign hangs together by the thinnest of threads, and liberal deus ex machina. Frequently you will look at the screen in confusion and ask "Who is that? What is happening? Why am I supposed to do this?" The game approaches storytelling in a very basic, almost childish way.
Even in my short time in the game, I have already encountered several borderline-gamebreaking bugs. Such as non-functional campaign triggers. And equally game-breaking, though no bug, is the games tendency to assume the player knows more that he does. This game needs a softer introduction, not to mechanics, but to world-building. As it is, it's a mess.
I am giving the developer the benefit of doubt, and I will continue playing. I do believe there is a lot of enjoyable content to come. But "it gets better later" is not a defence that a genuinely good game would need.
Let me put it like this: I am playing the game simply because it is the only game of its kind currently available. If it weren't for the fact that I have played Freelancer into the ground repeatedly, I would be playing that. It is a superior experience in every way.
Currently, I still regret spending money on this game. Therefore I am choosing not to recommend this game.
Update #1:
After a few more hours, I can only confirm my first impressions: I have absolutely no idea what is going on in the game, and my enjoyment of it suffers as a result. Time and time again, I am told I need to go to some place I don't know of, to meet a person I've never heard of, to get a thing which I know nothing about, for reasons that are never made clear. To call it frustrating is an understatement. The game is seemingly an unending series of unanswered questions. Primary among them: "Why am I doing this?"
This is not intentional mystery, this is just really, really bad writing.
Which is a damn, crying shame. Because the game itself, mechanics and graphics, are solid. Ish. A little shallow and clumsy, perhaps, but the closest I have come to Freelancer since Freelancer.
I wish this game was better. But it isn't. I wish I could love this game. But I can't.
I have given this game more than its fair share of chances. I have given it more than the benefit of doubt. I have acted on faith, on the belief and the hope, that this game "gets better". So far, this has proven to be wishful thinking.
I'll research the Gemini universe, and see if that gives me enough points of reference to piece together just what the hell is going on in the game. Then I'll give the game one last chance to pull itself out of this confusing funk and make some damn sense.
Update #2:
That helped a lot. A now have a fair grasp of what the game was assuming I knew by heart all along. It made the campaign bearable, though still not good by any measure. But at least I'm no longer tearing my hair out (as much) over the lack of proper world-building, exposition and adherence to storytelling 101.
I still can't recommend the game, despite that I am now beginning to enjoy it. Chances are that you won't be as patient as I have been, and I fail to muster any decent arguments as to why you would wish to be.

Alright, now that I've taken a couple deep breaths, let's analyse the experience so far. It's been 5 hours of enjoyable game play for me. The game is story rich, giving plenty of options to achieve your goals differently, this provides replay-ability value... BUT! As of right now, there is only 1 real, big mission and AFAIK there are 6 planned releases for the future. Well, that should stand for 6 more missions, which is sad IMHO, I loved the previous games, especially 2,3 and 4, with their open sandbox environment, multiple pathways, dozens of missions...
Multiplayer features could be a blast if implemented properly. A good idea would be for 2 players compete 1 vs the other in reaching the target first or blending in and eliminating one another, not the silly system that we see today. Elusive targets have little hopes, since it's a 1 time of a mission, that would allow a little more game-play in the same level that we already know by heart.
Bottom line: The game is promising, it would make much more sense to have more than 1 mission, even if the levels are 6 times smaller than what I saw today. If you are one of those patient people who would enjoy exploring 1 huge level and replay it many times, this game would be a good purchase. If you expect the same experience as the older games in the series, don't or you will be disappointed.
PS the menu controlls are a bit confusing as well.

Pros:
- large map

- challenges to add replay value
- more similar to original Hitman games

Cons:

- performance / connection issues
Neutral:

* With the connection issue at hand, I'm feeling more negative about upcoming elusive challenges.

FINAL EDIT: Things have changed. As of the November update, reward unlocks are now usable offline. Unfortunately, you still must be online when unlocking them, but you are now able to use your unlocked weapons, suits, starting locations, etc when offline. This is an acceptable compromise for me, and is enough to encourage me to change my review from not recommended to recommended.
Original review below:
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If you try to play offline, the game is stripped down to the most basic elements it could possibly be stripped down to. You can't even choose where you begin a mission if you're not logged in, let alone saves, browse equipment, create contracts, run escalation missions (obviously not having access to elusive targets makes sense)... oh, and god forbid you get disconnected or the servers have a brain fart while you're playing a mission...
However, I'm not at all unreasonable. I WANT to enjoy the game, but the strictly online-only features are a pretty big deal breaker for me. I really hope they get that sorted out, because this kind of garbage was supposed to have died with Assassin's Creed 2. There's no valid excuse for shutting out single-player features for players who aren't connected to the internet, and there's DEFINITELY no excuse for kicking players out of a single-player game for losing connection to the internet.
If they manage to fix that, I would switch to supporting the game entirely. I mean hell, I already paid $150 for a Steam code and a statue.
EDIT: Some things have changed since I wrote this review. IOI has applied some effort and made the game a little more manageable for players with inconsistent internet connections. For instance, an update was released that made it so that you are no longer taken back to the main menu as soon as your router dies or your internet connection experiences a hiccup. The game will now attempt to reconnect to the Hitman servers and allow you to keep playing.
However, this is not enough to make me change my review from not recommended to recommended. The game still will not allow you to earn or use unlocks, or access your saves (that were made while playing online) if you're not logged into the Hitman servers. While I do actually like Hitman, I can't in good conscience recommended a game that treats its players this way.
I still do not recomended purchasing Hitman.

Get Commandos 2 first. The learning curve here delicately holds your hand through the tutorial then hands you a live grenade and asks why you haven't defused it yet
The good news then, for veterans of the game, you'll really find your skills pushed here. Time is the big stricture here for many levels, where before you generally had the luxury of ticking off every enemy in your own time. Clearing a rail-field in minutes to intercept a train, with just the Green Beret, was an incredible level
In many respects, Commandos 3 improves upon the 2nd installment. The levels are smaller, so less onerous. The variety is also pushed so it's not just repetitions of "clear out this encampment". Quickly move to the front of a moving train, assassinate a traitor, destroy as many vehicles as possible before they leave the compound...
Ironically though, these work against it in some respects. The game is ridiculously short (compared to the previous titles) - there are only 12 levels in all, a handful of which take 5 minutes (if that), so you barely feel you get started with a campaign before it's over. Too many also become a bit "Commandos and Conquer" - less about stealth and more playing an RTS of hero units. They were fine in moderation in Commandos 2, but I felt they took up a few too many levels here
But whilst I say it's probably the least memorable of the 3 titles - The quality and challenge is still definitely there

Windward has that old school fun feeling. No one makes sailing games anymore and that a shame. Windward shows us just how much fun a modern sailing game is! It's a game that can deep in strategy, or hardcore action, or either casual. The choice is yours
You sail a ship and make profit in various ways so you can build a bigger ship with better cannons and sails. You also are part of a faction and your secondary goal is to protect your territory while expanding your factions territory. You do this buy capturing pirate held ports and also going to war with other factions.
When you first start off you'll probably spend a few hours just completing quests and buying/selling cargo for profit. Once you get a better ship the game starts to expand and your secondary objective becomes more realistic to you. This game is best played online, esp with friends, as taking over new territory is damn near impossible with just the AI's help.
A few positives:
Gorgeous water. It's just nice to look at.
Multiple things to do: There's trading, or Quests, or Improving your factions territory, or expanding your factions terrority, or Instances
Fun with friends. This game really shines with 3 or more friends
UI Upscale. You can actually play this from your couch as the UI has an option to upscale!! Few games allow this
Casual or Hardcore. This game comes with a difficulty slider to make the game easier or harder. But it also allows combat damage to be more or less. The interesting thing about this is your could play this game as a Trading sim on normal difficulty with low combat damage. Or lower the difficulty and increase the damage and you could do a Solo play as a lone conquerer. The choice is yours.
Cons
Slow gameplay. It's a sailing game. There's parts where you just sail. But also the beginning game can feel long and instances or capturing new territory can sometimes take too long as well. Especially since the AI for the enemy seems smarter than your own AI.
The tutorial. This one is iffy. The game tells you things, but you also discover things naturally. It is a good way to open the game up and much better than just dumbing 20 paragraphs of text at the beginning of a new player's start. However, the lack of information makes the start of the game slower. There are things you could do, that advanced players are doing, to get out of the starting territory and upgrade quicker, but the game sort of lets you discover that on your own.
Enemy AI. They tend to swarm up where your team's AI doesn't. It can be a real pain. I can't tell you how many times I've been left fighting 4 enemy ships while my team does f' all.
So yeah, great game! Lots of fun! A few complaints, but nothing terrible.

Lots of positive reviews on here convinced me to pick this one up while I wait for Star Citizen to drop. The comparisons to EVE are a joke and the two hold nearly nothing in common. Freelancer and Privateer? Sure. More recently, I'd compare this to Galaxy on Fire.
SG2 is nothing more than a sandbox space game. If that's all you want then you'll get a decent game. The interface and user experience could use a bit of work as well as additional options to sort/organize commodities and equipment. I honestly didn't expect it to reach version 1 in it's current state and really it could have benefited from several more months of dev time. Customization is very limited. Combat is fairly solid. You're free to do as you please, exploring the galaxy and making friends/enemies wherever you go.
I just wish there was something to drive the player beside their own goal. SG2 is lacking any sort of story. No big deal, it's a sandbox; I get it. Little story arc type missions would add so much though. Or a mission board to pick up missions in a more traditional fashion. Or the notion of of carrying out jobs for a particular company as a series of missions and work your way up. As it is, the game consists of flying around without direction, checking your map for freelance opportunities, accepting an opportunity, fly to the waypoint and either kill the badguy, or pick up and deliver cargo.  Mission done. Repeat until you can afford an ungodly expensive new ship and start again. They're the typical space game missions. It's a grind. And for me, if I'm going to grind at least give a me sense of purpose in doing so. Overall, this to me, is still a beta and was rushed out without any clear direction.

I originally owned this game on the first Xbox, where it was one of my most played games. While being backwards compatible with the Xbox 360 the game does not natively support a 360 controller, however, third party software such as Xpadder may be used to get around this, although there seems to be an issue with the game's use of the x-axis.
The story itself takes place after the Jedi Outcast games (which unfortunately I never played) with the player taking the role of an upcoming student under the tutilage of Kyle Katarn (protagonist of previous Jedi Knight games) at Luke Skywalker's academy on Yavin 4.
While the voice acting is sub-par, the game quickly gives you the ability to complete missions in the order of your chosing as well as allowing you to utilise different means to dispatch enemies. This means that despite being a Jedi padawan, the game still gives you the option of engaging with your enemies using weapons such as a blaster pistol or a bowcaster, as well as thermal detonators and trip mines. Combining these tools with force powers such as Grip, Pull and Push allow you to be 'creative' in your manner of killing.
All of this 'freedom' however is within a linear sandbox. The missions themselves dont all feel sequential and thus disconnected from the others, almost as if they are merely fillers between the main story missions. You could alternatively state that this is done in order to create an 'authentic' experience; under the guise of allowing you to choose the order of the missions given to you, the missions act as a means of learning how to effectively utilise the skills you have in order to be successful in the main missions which drive forward the narrative. As the story does progress, players have to option to level up force powers from both the Light and Dark sides respectively, which depending on which abilities you mostly use in a mission, earns a comment from either Luke or Kyle about how your objective was met. What I percieved to be the pinnacle of the game was when you accquired max level in all of your neutral force powers; at this time you were given the option to use a single, dual or a double bladed lightsaber - giving you access to amazingly stylised combinations of attack.
Multiplayer on this game is a confusing one for me. While it does support local bot play, there are some issues with connecting to servers. These range from not actually being able to find any, to the game freezing while you try to connect to one. Some of these issues may be due to either the server or the client your using having mods which conflict installed - this brings me to another point; mod support.
An outdated game such as this may turn people off solely due to the graphics. Well, for those that find this an issue, there are retexture packs out there for you to use install which do boost up the games appearance. There are also numerous mods for the game aswell; Movie Battles II and Knights of the Force are two I highly recommend you check out, as these increase the customisation of the lightsabers as well as giving you access to both locations and characters from the films.
Overall, I give this game an 8 out of 10. It's not the best Star Wars game I've played (that title belongs to KotOR) but it was the first Star Wars game I played which felt like I had a variety of ways to complete my objectives. For its time the combat was brilliant and provides an authentic Jedi experience.
WARNING: Towards the later stages of the game, players are faced with a choice (don't worry I wont spoil what it is). This choice however, appeared on screen in small text and for a short period of time. This may not be the case for the PC port, but I'd thought I'd give you a heads up in advance.

Following summary is just my opinion based on the current experience with the game.
Running on: Intel i5-750, nVidia GTX660 Ti, 16GB RAM and installed on storage HDD (5400 rpm)
PROS:
- game is looking pretty good even on my rig
- fast loading times
- stable
- many ways of taking out the target
- 47
- contracts
CONS:
- badly handled online protection
- story feels weak with this one
- not exactly wise way of releasing the game
While I recommend the game because there is a huge potential once all the missions are out, I strongly disagree with they way Square Enix has decided to release it - buying a game and getting it in pieces during the year does smell a bit. I do enjoy replaying the missions but not dozen times in a row. I prefer to play through, see the story and then go back and forth and replay missions in random order based on current mood.
My second complaint is about the always-online protection or whatever it is. Unlike many, I have no problem with such a feature as my connection rarely crashes. But, judging by the comments, in this case it's implemented just wrong. I'd expect the game to be able to switch to offline and let me play without the online features or at least save the game when it loses the connection and kicks me out so I can just jump back when it's all ok again. This is probably not the case tho. Game will just end and you've lost N minutes from the last save (autosave triggers often but still - WTF?).
I have no problems with performance, having 30-80 FPS in benchmark with 50 avg FPS. I'm also able to change anything in the settings, so I guess the HW limitations are based on the cards memory as I have a fairly old one. Whatever the reason is, it's a bad one - players should be able to mess up the game or burn down their HW if they want to :D Loading times are insanely fast, which is really surprising considering I have the game installed on 5400 rpm HDD with not-so-high speed of reading (other games are pain in the naughty bits when they have to load from this one).
If like me you don't have that much time to play, have other games to finish, don't mind paying for a full product but getting it over time or just trust SE that they won't screw with us, buy it. Once it's all out, it will be a great experience and you still can have a lot of fun with the provided contracts and even create your own.
If you're not comfortable with buying the game in this stage, wait few month until everything is released and then buy it. Or wait for some discount.
It's definitely worth the money but really needs some more love from developers to tweak the performance and that online thing. I also believe that minor updates with small side missions, new targets or new challenges for the existing ones would make the game more appealing because for skilled Hitman players there won't be much to do in a few days.

UPDATE: IO Interactive have now fully fleshed out the First Season of Hitman, and have finally optimized the game for PC. And let me just say this: I love this game, now. Everything about it that I complained about in the review below has been mostly fixed. The Opportunities now work far better. There are fewer bugs. And the new missions following Paris have been better and better. I absolutely love the new missions, and I love some of the features that were thrown at us following the initial mission releases (namely Elusive Targets and the Suit unlocks they allow). Bugs have been mostly nonexistant, and as I said above, the optimization is now perfect and is what I expected initially from this game. So I'm happy to update this to a Positive review, and definitely think you should go ahead and purchase at least the starter pack to see if you like the game and how well it runs, and then the Full Experience if you love it from there. I look forward to seeing what Season 2 has to offer.
IO Interactive have really stumbled upon something here. I believe they might have made a breakthrough in the gaming industry that no company has done since CryTek and CryEngine: IO Interactive have, somehow, made a game look horrible while making it the most demanding piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥you'll play in the coming years! Seriously, it's absolutely incredible how off (bad / mediocre) everything looks graphically, while running at sub 20 FPS on my system. My specs are becoming a little aged, I know, but they shouldn't be having so much trouble running this game even at medium on a medium resolution.
My specs:
CPU: Intel i7 4810MQ @ 2.8 GHz
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 780M with 4GB VRAM
RAM: 16GB
OS: Windows 8.1
HDD @ 750GB
SSD @ 250GB
This system can run The Division on High-Ultra at 1080p with about 40-50 FPS average
It runs Hitman at 720p on medium-low at about 17-20 FPS average.
All joking aside, I probably don't have to tell many of you reading this review how completely unbelievable this is. Hitman doesn't look good enough to be so demanding on my PC. It isn't worthy. But besides the performance issues and the Always-Online DRM issues, I believe Hitman has received the true return to form that it has deserved for a long time. With that return to form, though, comes some huge bugs that can make it difficult to feel like you're really walking in Agent 47's shoes. This game feels too much like a game - a buggy mess, at that.
I don't agree with the episodic release schedule (seriously, ♥♥♥♥ you Square Enix) but the missions that are available in the first episode so far have been pretty entertaining. There are limitless combinations for taking out the two targets you're assigned to kill in Paris. It is lots of fun sneaking around in Suit Only, and it is lots of fun using disguises (and knocking out guards) since you are no longer penalized for subduing people. Also, the new disguise system works extremely well, and allows for way more exploration than Absolution, which is great for a game like Hitman.
However, as I said, the gameplay isn't without its bugs. The new opportunities system has certainly added a lot to the game, and makes it much easier to experiment with the different things you can do to kill your targets. Of course, naturally, if you find it is too easy: you can turn it off. It's great. The problem is, though, that because of the way the game world works (Agent 47 has to be near an event / dialogue for it to happen) sometimes the opportunities don't actually work very well, and lead to some frustrating instances where the target is running around spouting nonsense and failing to do what needs to be done by their AI, because their AI is playing catchup now that Agent 47 is nearby. There are also numerous other little bugs that I've encountered already. Nothing too gamebreaking, but still extremely annoying:
In The Final Test, I approached Jasper Knight to get him to follow me as part of one of the opportunities. When he finished his scripted dialogue, he suddenly ran through about 8 lines of phrases like "Are we going or what?" "Hello, grease monkey?" "C'mon, I don't have all day!" and went back to what he was doing like I hadn't even been there. It became evident that his AI somehow got the notion that we'd been standing there for 20 minutes instead of 10 seconds, and set him back on his regularly scheduled programming. Which didn't impact the mission too much, as it worked perfectly the next time, but it was still extremely odd and removed me from the immersion of the game.
In Showstopper, I stole Helmut Kruger's (the supermodel who looks like Agent 47) disguise and was meeting up with the second target, who wanted to see Helmut in a specific place upstairs. I went to that place and sat for about 10 minutes, watching the target go from place to place in Instinct mode. When I had had enough, I approached the target - and she didn't even acknowledge me. I couldn't speak to her, like I had spoken to Jasper. The only time she would notice me was when I stood directly in her path, and her AI got annoyed and told me to move, not recognizing her close personal friend, Helmut. 10 more minutes pass, and I managed to close the auction with some hacking on her laptop. I thought this would let her and Helmut meet, but it didn't. Instead, she proceeded to storm through me (while recognizing me as two people at once - Helmut Kruger, and Tobias Reaper, which is the alias Agent 47 uses if you manage to sneak into the auction in your suit without using a disguise). Again, it completely ruined my immersion, and because of the failure for the event to spark, it made it nearly impossible to kill the target in the way I wanted to without blowing my cover.
It is my personal opinion, that if any quality assurance had been done at all on this game, then both of these bugs would have been easily detected. I didn't do anything to trigger them except by playing the game. Things like this should not be happening for no other reason than shoddy programming. It's completely ridiculous for such a huge title. I really was excited for this game, because I finally believed IO was going to get it right - but they didn't. It almost seems like they just crapped out what they could so they could grab some cash from Hitman's most loyal fans. I'm praying that one day I can turn this review into a positive one. But until they actually optimize the game for PCs that should be able to run it, and fix the glaring bugs that are evident everywhere in the game world, I just can't recommend buying Hitman in any other form, not even just the First Episode.

When you are level one, you have almost no skills, no stat points, and no idea how to play. By the time you reach level ~15, you have a basic understanding of the game.
Then starts the next problem, after 1-23, you have 23-50.
Then you start to regret playing the game. Community is extremely toxic since you play with your level 24 against people who could have hundreds of hours on the game over you. All of the skills unlock at 24 but you need in-game points to buy them, something you need to play a lot to buy. Even if you were to buy them all, you need to level up to get the skill-slots. Most of the time you will get stomped on in whatever role you chose, get made-fun-of by your teammates and called a noob and worthless. You will not learn anything unless you meet the rare 1/50 nice person who will play with you anyway. Most of the time, you go back and make a new character, just to play in the low level server again.
If you decide to go through the game with friends, it will make the experience slightly better. Only thing is you and your friends have to dedicate to losing a lot. It takes dedication to get better in this game, learning the jank controls and precise timing (especially if you don't have a ping of under 50.) That dedication can certainly be broken by losing to P2W characters non-stop for a whole night.
Also, the game is P2W. You get more stat points for purchasing special characters and more stats for buying points on your clothes. Pay money, get better/more stat points. Also, the game is dictated by what skills you attach, and you can pay to get more skill slots therefore have an even bigger advantage.
I would avoid this unless you have two friends who enjoy sports games.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is that rare thing, a strong sim tethered to a strong game. Where other vehicle-obsessed devs seem to take player motivation for granted, Czech studio SCS understand that a pleasingly modelled steed needs a pleasingly modelled environment to shine.
On this occasion that environment is a swathe of Europe stretching from Plymouth in the west to Wroclaw in the east, from Aberdeen in the north to Milan in the South. The tangle of motorways and major roads is stylised and condensed, but feels massive. After a splendid week of non-stop trucking the stats screen tells me I've still only seen 50% of it.
There's satisfaction in exploring new routes, seeing new golden been-there-done-that squiggles appearing on the in-game map, but it tends to be the promise of cold, hard cash that gets you out of bed in the morning. Like Farming Simulator, ETS2 has a simple yet resonant economic sandbox at its centre.
You start as a low-skilled, truckless lorry jockey, forced to take work from established haulage companies. Slowly (or rapidly if you go to a bank) you amass the funds to buy your first rig and rent your first yard. Then the fun really begins. Contract perusing, truck pimping, skill upgrading, driver hiring... this is Eddie Stobart: The Game in all but name.
Spending 90 minutes ferrying a tank of propane from Sheffield to Prague could (should?) be tedious. The fact that it isn't is largely down to good-if-not-quite-OMSI-standard physics, and varied road layouts and scenery. Periods of smooth, almost soporific motorway motoring nestle between passages of edgier wheelwork. One minute you're cruising along contemplating the sunset over the central reservation, the next you're on a rain-lashed country road at night, waiting for the right moment to pass a painfully slow pantechnicon. Tiredness can't kill in ETS2, but it can leave you jack-knifed in a ditch, feeling awful with a substantial repair bill to pay.

I'm up to around 60 hours of playtime now and I have my first $2 million prison with over 350 inmates. Yesterday I expanded across the road for the first time.
The gameplay has much variety to it, as you can build the prison any way you want and run it how you see fit. It can be tuned more twoard punishment with many armed guards and basic cells, or the goal can be reform, with many programs to help inmates get relase early. Some prisons are visually pleasing, while others are efficient and functional, but ugly.
On my currnet prison, with 350 inmates and around 200 staff members, I find the game lags some. I have a FX-6300 CPU and 16GB of RAM, but I understand the game runs on only a single core.
The biggest bug I see is installing electrical lines in a larger prison. I have six or seven power stations, and almost every time I add to my power lines I get a "no route" error. I don't understand that as the work men have a clear route to the work site. Sometimes it'll take me 10 minutes to add maybe 20 squares of power lines, which is very frustrating. I hope IV addresses that in a patch.
I plan to continue playing my currnet prison until I feel it's maxed out. I really enjoy the game, but my wife hates that I spent two or three hours at a time playing.
